January 2, 1938. Morning Translation.

Ta hei Wan Pao Morning Edition and other local newspapers .-

HAND-GRENADES THROWN AT JAPANESE SOLDIERS ON
HANKOW ROAD; KILLS IN WESTERN DISTRICT ATTACKED

Between 11 a.m. and 12.30 p.m. yesterday, four
cases of attacks by hand-grenades occurred in the
International Settlement.
The most serious one occurred at about 11.23 a.m.,
on Hankow Road west of Fokien Road, where a party of 70
or 80 Japanese soldiers were sight-seeing. Two loud
explosions were heard, followed by three more shortly
afterwards. The explosions resulted in the wounding of
four Japanese soldiers, one of them in the head, the
wounds of the other three being slight, also five Chinese
civilians, of whom four were slightly wounded and the
fifth, a woman, more seriously, necessitating her
detention in the Lester Chinese Hospital. When our
reporter visited the scene at 3 p.m., he saw two small
holes in the road.
Immediately after the incident, a police party
attended to make investigations. Traffic was suspended
and emergency measures were adopted in the area.
The thrower or throwers of the hand-grenades are
still unknown. A foreigner who was passing the spot in
a ricksha at the time of the incident stated that he
personally saw a person wearing Japanese military uniform
throw the missile, but whether this person had not been a
disguised non-Japanese subject or whether the foreigner's
statement is correct is open to doubt.
The Police have found a number of fragments from
the missiles; these will be examined. The Police also
took photographs of the scene of the incident and its
vicinity. Shops nearby were searched but with no result.
After the explosion, the Japanese soldiers took liberty of
action and searched the pedestrians. Representatives of
the Japanese naval and military authorities and of the
Japanese Consulate also attended to make enquiries. The
precautionary measures in that area were removed at 3.25p.m.
when the Police and the Japanese authorities completed
their enquiries. After this, many groups of Japanese
in two's and three's were seen to walk about on the
streets nearby for some time.
The other three cases occurred in the Western
District of the Settlement. They are reported as follows:
(1) At about 11.20 a.m. two Chinese threw two hand
grenades at the Cotton Mill, 74 Robinson Road, only one
of them exploding.. The Italian marines stationed in the
mill opened fire and the Chinese replied. There were no
casualties and the two Chinese made good their escape.
(2) At about 11.50 a.m. a Chinese threw two hand-
grenades at the King Dah Mill, 98 Singapore Road, both
of which exploded. A Chinese was wounded. The Italian
marines stationed there fired two shots, but the thrower
of the hand-grenades made good his escape.

手榴弹投向汉口路上的日本士兵；西区袭击致人伤亡

昨日上午11时至下午12时30分之间，公共租界内发生了四起手榴弹袭击事件。
最严重的一起发生在上午11时23分左右，地点位于福建路以西的汉口路，当时有一队约七八十名日本士兵正在观光。听到两声巨响，随后不久又传来三声。爆炸导致四名日本士兵受伤，其中一人头部受伤，另外三人伤势较轻；另有五名中国平民受伤，其中四人轻伤，第五名是一名妇女，伤势较重，需留院治疗于莱斯中国医院（Lester Chinese Hospital）。本报记者于下午3时抵达现场时，看到路面上有两个小洞。
事发后，警方立即前往调查。该区域交通中断，并采取了紧急措施。
投掷手榴弹者身份尚不明。一名外国人称，事发时他正乘坐人力车经过该地，亲眼看到一名身穿日本军服的人投掷了爆炸物，但此人是否为非日本籍人士伪装，或者该外国人的陈述是否属实，仍存疑。
警方在现场发现了多块手榴弹碎片；这些碎片将接受检查。警方还拍摄了事发地点及其周边的照片。对附近商店进行了搜查，但一无所获。
爆炸发生后，日本士兵自行行动，搜查行人。日本海陆军当局及日本领事馆的代表也到场进行问询。下午3时25分，当警方和日本当局完成问询后，该区域的预防措施被解除。此后，一段时间内可以看到许多成群结队的日本人，两三人一组，在附近街道上走动。
另外三起案件发生在租界西区。报告如下：
(1) 上午11时20分左右，两名中国人向罗宾森路74号的棉纺厂投掷了两枚手榴弹，仅一枚爆炸。驻守在该厂的意大利海军陆战队开火，中国人予以还击。无人伤亡，两名中国人成功逃脱。
(2) 上午11时50分左右，一名中国人向新加坡路98号的金达纱厂（King Dah Mill）投掷了两枚手榴弹，均爆炸。一名中国人受伤。驻守在那里的意大利海军陆战队开了两枪，但投掷手榴弹者成功逃脱。

At 11.30 p.m. 1-1-38, (i.e. .).1944 walking 3 and
4 beats :: section reported by telephone that hand-
grenades had been thrown on Hankow Road, near Fokien
Road and that there were many Japanese soldiers there.
Chief Inspector Theobald and all available
men immediately proceeded to the scene. Mr. Robertson
J.P., A.D.C. also attended. All traffic with exception
of trams and railless buses was diverted and on
arrival of the Reserve Unit a systematic search of
surrounding shops, houses and looking houses was
carried out by uniform and detective parties.
Enquiries by S.I. Sharma, S.I. Ma Hon,
S.I. Hardie, S.I. Chang Yuen Chi, and other
members of the detective staff elicited that a
party of about 34 Japanese soldiers led by J. O.
112 on a night cooling walking tour (one of many such
parties observed walking in the district) were walk-
ing out on Hankow Road and at about 11.30 p.m. when
they were about 10 yards West of Fokien Road, two
hand-grenades of the Chinese Military type were
thrown from a group of Chinese standing on the South
West corner of Hankow and Fokien Roads. Both grenades
exploded near the centre of Hankow Road, upon which
the crowds in the vicinity scattered in all directions.
The Japanese soldiers ran West on Hankow Road and
turned South on North Road, but on seeing dense
crowds, Sergeant Kaneko drew his pistol and fired 4
rounds from his .38 auto pistol, (- cross sound)
without apparently hitting any one. The soldiers

1938年1月1日晚上11时30分（即...），第3和第4巡区的警员通过电话报告称，在汉口路近福建路处有人投掷手榴弹，那里有许多日本士兵。
总督察西奥博尔德（Theobald）和所有可用警力立即赶赴现场。太平绅士、副官罗伯逊先生（Mr. Robertson J.P., A.D.C.）也到场。除电车和无轨巴士外，所有交通均被改道，预备队到达后，制服警员和便衣警员对周围的商店、房屋和寄宿处进行了系统搜查。
经警探夏尔马（Sharma）、警探马 Hon（Ma Hon，音译）、警探哈迪（Hardie）、警探张元志（Chang Yuen Chi，音译）及其他便衣人员的问询得知，一支由 J. O. 112 率领的约34名日本士兵组成的队伍正在进行夜间散步降温活动（这是在该地区观察到的众多此类队伍之一），他们正走在汉口路上，大约在晚上11时30分，当他们走到福建路以西约10码处时，两枚中国式军用型手榴弹从站在汉口路和福建路西南角的一群中国人中投出。两枚手榴弹均在汉口路中央附近爆炸，随后周围人群向四面八方散开。日本士兵沿汉口路向西跑，然后在北路向南转，但看到密集的人群后，金子警长（Sergeant Kaneko）拔出手枪，用他的.38口径自动手枪发射了4发子弹，（- 交叉声）显然未击中任何人。士兵们

of Chinese standing watching the Japanese soldiers pass
by. When the soldiers had almost passed he heard two
explosions and saw the people scatter. He also noticed
the leaflets before mentioned, being thrown into the
air, but is unable to give any description of the
persons throwing them. Neither is he able to give
descriptions of any of the group who were standing on
t. footpath at the time the Japanese were passing.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Nothing resulted from the search of shops,
dwelling houses, hotels and lodging houses and the
Japanese officials withdrew at about 3.15 The Reserve

Detectives remained on the scene and continued

houses, refugee camps and hospitals, especially as to
the source of the leaflets found at the scene.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No. ......
                                Louza ......... Station,
            REPORT              Date January 1, 19 37.
Subject Hand Grenades thrown at Japanese Soldiers Fukien & Hankow Roads.

Made by ............ and, .................... Forwarded by Chief Inspector Shellsell.

Sir,
    Reference to the attached I beg to report that at about
11.25 a.m. 1/1/38 a message was received at the station from
C.P.C.1544 reporting that hand grenades had been thrown at a
party of Japanese soldiers whilst passing the corner of Fukien
& Hankow Roads. Chief Inspector Shellsell, Inspectors
MacFarlane and Liu Ya Ying immediately proceeded there. On
reaching Kiukiang and Hoopeh Roads corner a party of Japanese
soldiers numbering about 30 were seen running North along
Hoopeh Road and turned East along Kiukiang Road. One Japanese
soldier was seen to fire a shot into the air. On proceeding
South along Hoopeh Road I observed 3 or 4 Japanese soldiers,
two of whom appeared to be wounded. Inspector MacFarlane
stopped a car which was proceeding South along Hoopeh Road
and took the two Japanese soldiers along to the Lester Hospital.
    At this time 9 Japanese soldiers had taken refuge in a
silk store situated No. 255 Hoopeh Road. I immediately went
inside and spoke to one of them who understood a little
English, telling them not to venture out on the street, but
to stay in the shop and I would see that no harm came to them.
I then rang Sub Inspector Willis on Charge Room duty and
informed him to let D.O. "A" and D.D.O. "A" know of what
had occurred. All traffic was stopped and the area cleared
of all Chinese.
    D.O. "A", D.D.O. "A" immediately attended with C.D.I.
Sherman and a party of detectives. A search of hotels and
lodging houses in vicinity at once carried out.
    Reserve Unit later attended and carried out searches
of premises and pedestrians on the streets.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。    档案号 ......
                                老闸 ......... 分局，
            报告              日期 19 37年1月1日。
主题 在福建路与汉口路向日本士兵投掷手榴弹。

由 ............ 和, .................... 制作。由总督察Shellsell转呈。

先生，
    参照附件，谨此报告，1938年1月1日上午约11时25分，本局接到中央巡捕房1544号来电，报告称一群日本士兵在经过福建路与汉口路转角时遭到手榴弹袭击。总督察Shellsell、督察MacFarlane和刘亚英立即前往该处。到达九江路与湖北路转角时，看见一群约30人的日本士兵沿湖北路向北奔跑，随后沿九江路向东转弯。看见一名日本士兵向空中开了一枪。沿湖北路向南行进时，我观察到3或4名日本士兵，其中两人似乎受伤。MacFarlane督察拦下一辆沿湖北路向南行驶的汽车，将两名日本士兵送往莱斯特医院（Lester Hospital）。
    此时，9名日本士兵躲藏在位于湖北路255号的一家丝绸店内。我立即进入店内，与其中一名懂一点英语的士兵交谈，告诉他们不要冒险走到街上，而是留在店内，我会确保他们不受伤害。随后我打电话给值班室的副督察Willis，通知他告知“A”区值班官和“A”区副值班官发生的情况。所有交通被阻断，该区域内的所有华人被清空。
    “A”区值班官、“A”区副值班官立即会同刑事侦缉处主任Sherman及一队侦探到场。立即对附近的旅馆和寄宿处进行了搜查。
    后备队随后到场，并对街道上的处所和行人进行了搜查。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............
Central Station,
REPORT
Date Jan. 1st, 1938.

Subject (in full) Japanese soldiers sightseeing in Central
and Louza Districts.

Made by Inspt. Papp. Forwarded by [Signature] [Signature]

Sir,
During the forenoon, January, 1st, 1938, several groups
of Japanese soldiers, usually under the command of an officer,
entered the Central District via Garden Bridge with the
apparent purpose of sightseeing. They walked in twos and
were armed with bayonets but no rifles. After entering the
District, most of the groups walked along the Bund and then
turned into Nanking Road. Others walked along the Bund and
turned into Peking Road. All groups after crossing the
Central District proceeded into the Louza District. The
groups returned via the roads mentioned.

At about 11.20 a.m., Jan. 1st 1938, one large group
about 80 Japanese soldiers was escorted by the undersigned
along Nanking and Sianse Roads to the District boundary, at
corner of Hankow Road, where the group proceeded west along
Hankow Road into the Louza District.

The undersigned has exchanged greetings with several of
the groups and the soldiers appeared to be quite friendly.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently.

(Signed) H. Papp
Inspector

主题（全称）日本士兵在中央区和老闸区观光。

由Papp督察制作。由 [签名] [签名] 转呈

先生，
1938年1月1日上午，几群日本士兵，通常由一名军官指挥，经由外白渡桥进入中央区，其目的显然是观光。他们两人一组行走，配备刺刀但未携带步枪。进入该区后，大多数队伍沿外滩行走，然后转入南京路。其他队伍沿外滩行走，然后转入北京路。所有队伍在穿过中央区后都进入了老闸区。各队伍经上述道路返回。

1938年1月1日上午约11时20分，一大群约80名日本士兵由卑职护送，沿南京路和山西路行进至位于汉口路转角的区界，该队伍随后沿汉口路向西进入老闸区。

卑职已与几支队伍互致问候，士兵们显得十分友好。

先生，
您顺从的。

（签名）H. Papp

page_data.en:
R.M. Carlen, residing 1140/17 Bubbling
Well Road.                                      self
         Portuguese
Louga Station           1-1-38

On the 1st of January 1938, whilst I was proceeding West
on Nankow Road, on my way to the Shanghai Races on the office
private ricksha. Just before reaching Pekien and Nankow Roads
Corner at 11:30 a.m. I heard two loud explosion and West of
Pekien Road hundreds of people running wild in all directions.
I immediately stop my ricksha to investigate what have happened
as I knew for experience in my services in C.M.P. Specials that
it is a bomb.

I saw one Japanese marine, one Chinese ricksha coolie and
a Chinese lad was wounded. I immediately rang for our ambulance
and same time notify the Stations. The ambulance came and the
three wounded sent to Lester Hospital. C.C.3188 who is on
Point duty at the Corner of Keepch and Nankow Roads came running
to the scene of explosion withdrawn pistol. I did not see who
threw the bomb. A few minutes later, I saw about 50 to 60
Japanese marines crossing Keepch Road in double march.

Before I heard the explosion I did not see any Japanese
in the vicinity as the streets were very crowded with
pedestrians and other traffic.

Signed: R.M. Carlen.
page_data.zh:
R.M. Carlen，居住于静安寺路1140/17号。                                      本人
         葡萄牙籍
老闸分局           1938年1月1日

1938年1月1日，当我乘坐办公用私人黄包车前往上海跑马厅时，正沿南京西路向西行进。上午11时30分，就在即将到达北京路与南京路转角之前，我听到两声巨大的爆炸声，在北京路以西，数百人四处疯狂奔逃。我立即停下黄包车调查发生了什么，因为我在公共租界特别巡捕队服役的经验让我知道这是炸弹。

我看见一名日本海军陆战队员、一名中国黄包车夫和一名中国少年受伤。我立即呼叫我们的救护车，同时通知各分局。救护车赶到，三名伤者被送往莱斯特医院。在江西路与南京路转角执行定点任务的3188号华捕跑向爆炸现场，拔出手枪。我没有看到是谁投掷了炸弹。几分钟后，我看见约50至60名日本海军陆战队员双列纵队穿过江西路。

在听到爆炸声之前，我没有看到附近有任何日本人，因为街道上挤满了行人和其他车辆。

签名：R.M. Carlen。

page_data.en:
C.F.C.1596 Tsang Zang Ying (    ),
D.S. Miscell.
unihli
Louza Station        1-1-38

My name is Tsang Zang Ying, C.P.C.1596 attached to Louza
Station.

At 11.15.a.m. 1-1-38 I was on traffic duty at Hankow and
Fokien Roads corner at this time I noticed many uniformed
Japanese soldiers walking and sat on Hankow Road near
Fokien Road in the middle of the road. accompanied by J.P.S.112
I was standing on the north side of Hankow Road looking south
on Fokien Road, and had stopped the north & south bound traffic
in order to allow the soldiers to cross the intersection. When
they had all passed the intersection I heard a loud noise, but
I did not know what had caused the noise until I heard someone
say that a bomb had been thrown, in the meantime the Japanese
soldiers and all the passersby had scattered in all directions.
I immediately proceeded to the Yan T'ong (    ) Clothing shop,
231 Fokien Road, from which place I telephoned to the station
informing the sub-inspector-on-duty of the occurrence.

After telephoning to the station I returned to the scene
and was approached by a ricksha coolie one, Yam Shou Ding (
84, Tsungning, No.10 Rue Sants, ricksha S.K.C. Lic. 6635, who
informed me that he had seen a Japanese soldier take a bomb from
his pocket and throw it on the roadway, I therefore immediately
brought the man to the station as a witness.

Owing to the fact that the intersection where I was
stationed is very busy and had a large flow of traffic at that
particular time I did not see the bomb thrown nor did I see any
pamphlets being thrown on to the roadway.

(Signed) Tsang Zang Ying.
page_data.zh:
中央巡捕房1596号 Tsang Zang Ying (        )，
杂务股
unihli
老闸分局        1938年1月1日

我叫Tsang Zang Ying，系隶属老闸分局的中央巡捕房1596号巡捕。

1938年1月1日上午11时15分，我正在汉口路与福建路转角执行交通勤务，当时我注意到许多身穿制服的日本士兵在汉口路靠近福建路的马路中间行走和坐着。在日本特别巡捕112号的陪同下，我站在汉口路北侧，面向南注视福建路，并阻断了南北向交通，以便让士兵们穿过路口。当他们全部通过路口后，我听到一声巨响，但在听到有人说投掷了炸弹之前，我不知道是什么造成了噪音，与此同时，日本士兵和所有行人都向四面八方散开。我立即前往福建路231号的Yan T'ong (        ) 服装店，从那里打电话给分局，向值班副督察报告了此事。

给分局打完电话后，我回到现场，一名叫Yam Shou Ding ( 84岁，住同宁路10号，黄包车牌照S.K.C. 6635) 的黄包车夫走近我，告诉我他看见一名日本士兵从口袋里拿出一颗炸弹扔在马路上，因此我立即将该人作为证人带到分局。

由于我驻守的路口非常繁忙，且当时交通流量很大，我没有看到炸弹被投掷，也没有看到任何传单被扔到马路上。

（签名）Tsang Zang Ying。

page_data.en:
Tsai Tsoong Zen (        ), C.P.W.490,
Shantung                                D.S. Kao Adie.
Louza Station    1-1-38                 D.I. Loh Kung Fung.

My name is Tsai Tsoong Zen (        ), age 41, native of
Shantung. I am C.P.W.490 unarmed stationed at the Yun Tsong
(        ) Clothing shop, 231 Fokien Road at the corner of Hankow
Road. I am on duty from 10.a.m. to 9.p.m. each day. At 10.a.m.
1-1-38 I came on duty and took up my usual place at the doorway
of the shop. At 10.30.a.m. I left the shop and came to Louza
Station to have my conference book signed, this being done every
Saturday. I returned to the shop at about 10.55.a.m. and sat in
the shop in my chair at the back of a glass case. At about 11.15
a.m. as far as I remember I heard shouts from people on the road-
way saying "Japanese soldiers coming" I then got up and stood in
the open doorway of the shop. By that time I saw that about
twenty Japanese soldiers walking from east to west had just
passed the door of my shop, 5 or 6 Japanese soldiers were on the
opposite corner of Hankow and Fokien Road looking at fur coats in
a shop while behind were 20 or 30 more Japanese soldiers. The
soldiers were all armed with swords and were not marching but
walking in small groups at once. At the same time, I saw a
number of Chinese pedestrians walking along the road while about
seven or eight Chinese were standing on the pavement outside my
shop. After I had stood in the doorway about 2 or 3 seconds I
heard two explosions almost simultaneously and saw black smoke
arising from the middle of Hankow Road about 3 or 4 yards west of
Fokien Road. By this time most of the Japanese with the excep-
tion of 4 or 5 had passed the spot westwards. Everybody on the
roadway including the Japanese scattered in all directions away
from the scene and the roadway was cleared except for one Chinese
page_data.zh:
Tsai Tsoong Zen (        )，华捕490号，
山东籍                                高级探员 Kao Adie。
老闸分局    1938年1月1日                 侦探长 Loh Kung Fung。

我叫Tsai Tsoong Zen (        )，41岁，山东籍。我是无武装的华捕490号，驻守在汉口路转角的福建路231号Yun Tsong (        ) 服装店。我每天执勤时间为上午10时至晚上9时。1938年1月1日上午10时，我上岗并在店门口占据 usual 位置。上午10时30分，我离开店铺来到老闸分局签署会议记录簿，这是每周六都要做的。上午约10时55分我回到店里，坐在玻璃柜台后面的一把椅子上。据我所记，上午约11时15分，我听到路上有人喊“日本兵来了”，于是我起身站在店铺敞开的门口。那时我看到大约二十名日本士兵从东向西走过，刚经过我的店门，5或6名日本士兵在汉口路与福建路对面的转角处观看一家店里的皮大衣，后面还有20或30名日本士兵。士兵们都佩带军刀，并非列队行进，而是分成小组行走。同时，我看见许多中国行人在路上行走，约有七八名中国人站在我店外的人行道上。我在门口站了约2或3秒后，几乎同时听到两声爆炸，看见黑烟从汉口路中间升起，位置在福建路以西约3或4码处。此时，除4或5人外，大多数日本人已向西经过该地点。路上的所有人，包括日本人，都从现场向四面八方散开，路面被清空，只剩下一名中国

page_data.en:
Sheet No.2

female lying on the north west footpath by the pillar box and
a ricksha coolie sitting on the pavement on the south west
corner. As the pedestrians ran southwards along Nanking Road
I saw some leaflets fluttering downwards in the air, the highest
being about six or seven feet from the ground. They were evi-
dently thrown by some person who was across a house but I did not
actually see them thrown. This spot is about six yards from
the south west corner of Nanking Road at the edge of the west
pavement of Nanking Road. I did not see any bombs thrown but
when I saw two panes of glass broken in the shop I realized that
bombs had exploded. A few moments later a Japanese Police
Sergeant Wells ran up to my shop from Hankow Road west and
asked to use the telephone. I escorted him to the first floor
where he telephoned from the shop's booth. After that I went
downstairs to look after the shop as all the assistants had run
away. I cannot describe any of the Chinese waiting on the pavement
but none of the persons in my sight threw the bombs.
This is my true statement.
(Signed) Tsai Tseeng Yen.
page_data.zh:
第2页

女子躺在西北侧人行道上的邮筒旁，以及一名黄包车夫坐在西南角的人行道上。当行人沿南京路向南奔跑时，我看见一些传单在空中飘落，最高处离地面约六七英尺。它们显然是由某个在房子对面的人投掷的，但我并没有亲眼看到它们被投掷。该地点距离南京路西南角约六码，位于南京路西侧人行道的边缘。我没有看到任何炸弹被投掷，但当我看到店里有两块玻璃破碎时，我意识到炸弹已经爆炸。片刻之后，一名日本警长Wells从汉口路西侧跑到我的店里，要求使用电话。我陪他到二楼，他在店里的电话间打了电话。之后我下楼照看店铺，因为所有店员都跑掉了。我无法描述在人行道上等候的任何中国人，但我视线范围内没有人投掷炸弹。
这是我的真实陈述。
（签名）Tsai Tseeng Yen。

page_data.en:
J.P.S.112 Shigeo Aida. (temporarily attached
Hongkew)
JAPAN.                                         Self.      Witnessed by
Louza Station           1-1-38                              J.D.S. Kobayashi.

Sir,
    I beg to report that I was detailed on duty at the Garden
Bridge from 8.a.m. to 5.p.m. 1-1-38. At about 11.10.a.m. 1-1-38
I was instructed by Sub Inspector Shimizu to escort 54 Japanese
soldiers carrying only bayonets to Central District for the
purpose of sight seeing. They were requested by one of the
Japanese Gendarmarie on duty at the Garden Bridge to Sub Inspec-
tor Kinamiya.
    I left the Garden Bridge at 11.20.a.m. walking at the front
I proceeded along the Bund, turning into Nanking Road near
Henan Road, 5 or 6 Japanese soldiers attached themselves to the
party which I was leading. When I approached the corner of
Nanking & Shanxi Roads, one of the warrant officers wished to
turn to Shanxi Road for the purpose of looking at local Chinese
shops. I complied with his request and turned south along Shanxi
Road. Reaching the intersection of Hankow and Shanxi Roads, they
wished to go to the Race Course, and we turned to Hankow Road.
I was still leading the party in front.
    Passing the corner of Hankow and Fukien Roads, and approa-
ching the corner of Seeyah Road, I heard a sudden explosion in the
rear, when I turned back I saw a flash in the air like that of
electricity over on the south side of Hankow Road. I immediately
ran to the scene to make enquiries at this time my watch gave the
hour as 11.38.a.m. I saw one of the soldiers attached to the
party which I was leading, had been wounded by some missile. All
those persons on the roadway had by this time dispersed, therefore
I immediately made my way to a Chinese shopkeeper who was standing
page_data.zh:
J.P.S.112 相田茂雄。（临时配属虹口）
日本。                                         本人。      见证人
老闸捕房           1938年1月1日                              J.D.S. 小林。

先生：
    谨此报告，我于1938年1月1日上午8时至下午5时在花园桥执勤。约在1938年1月1日上午11时10分，清水巡佐指示我护送54名仅携带刺刀的日本士兵前往中区观光。这是由一名在花园桥执勤的日本宪兵向木宫巡佐提出的请求。
    我于上午11时20分离开花园桥，走在队伍前面，沿外滩行进，在河南路附近转入南京路，有5或6名日本士兵加入了我带领的队伍。当我接近南京路与山西路的转角时，其中一名士官希望转入山西路，以便观看当地中国商店。我应其请求，沿山西路向南转弯。到达汉口路与山西路交汇处时，他们希望去跑马厅，于是我们转入汉口路。我仍然在队伍前方领路。
    经过汉口路与福建路转角，接近四川路转角时，我听到身后突然发生爆炸，当我回头时，我看到汉口路南侧空中有一道类似电光的闪光。我立即跑往现场进行查问，此时我的手表显示时间为上午11时38分。我看到一名加入我所带领队伍的士兵被某种抛射物击伤。此时道路上的所有人员均已散开，因此我立即走向一名站在

page_data.en:
Sheet No.2.

side of Hankow Road, for the purpose of reporting the occurrence
and on entering I met a C.I.C.1590 whom I requested to telephone
for the ambulance, I, myself, then tried to communicate with
Hongkew Police Station by telephone but was unable to do so.
When I left the shop I saw that the ambulance had already
arrived, and I escorted the wounded Japanese soldiers to
the Lester Chinese Hospital, Szechung Road. On arriving at the
above hospital I also encountered a person, soldier and a female
Chinese who had also been wounded at Hankow and Fokien Roads
corner.

（签名）
U.S.S. 118.
page_data.zh:
第2页。

汉口路一侧的中国店主处，目的是报告此事，进入店内后，我遇到了一名编号为C.I.C.1590的华籍警员，我请他打电话叫救护车，随后我自己试图通过电话与虹口捕房联系，但未能接通。当我离开店铺时，我看到救护车已经到达，我便护送受伤的日本士兵前往四川路的莱斯忒华人医院（Lester Chinese Hospital）。到达上述医院时，我还遇到了一名同样在汉口路与福建路转角受伤的士兵和一名中国女性。

（签名）
U.S.S. 118.

page_data.en:
Yeh Kwai Sai (馬桂小), S.P.C.3188.
Self.
Louza Stn. 1-1-38 Interp. Gilang.

My name is Mak Kwai San. C.P.C.3188 attached to Louza Stn.
At 11.20 a.m. 1-1-38 when I was on duty at the intersection
of Hupeh & Hankow Roads, I noticed about 20 Japanese soldiers,
accompanied by a J.P.C. walking along Hankow Road, West of
Fokien Road, proceeding East. Accordingly I cleared the roadway
of traffic and pedestrians in order to allow the soldiers to
cross the intersection. When they had all passed the intersec-
tion, I heard two explosions. The Japanese soldiers at once ran
towards Hupeh and Hankow Roads, and I dispersed all the pedes-
trians on the roadway, having drawn my service pistol, and ran
to the scene of the incident. On arriving, I noticed C.P.C.1506
who was on duty at Hankow and Fokien Roads, go to the Van Tsong
( ), where he informed the station by telephone. A Inspr.
of the Specials, in civilian clothes, also attended the scene.
I then conveyed the wounded soldiers and pedestrians from
the roadway to the pavement, when the traffic was stopped for a
few minutes.
Later staff from the station arrived on the scene and I
returned to my post at about 11.40 a.m.
On Hupeh Road, about 30 yards north of Hankow Road, on the
west side pavement, I found a piece of shrapnel, which has been
handed over to the Chief Inspector S/S.
This is my true statement.
(Signed) Mak Kwai San.
page_data.zh:
叶桂生（馬桂小），S.P.C.3188。
本人。
老闸捕房 1938年1月1日 翻译：Gilang。

我叫麦桂三（Mak Kwai San）。编号C.P.C.3188，配属老闸捕房。
1938年1月1日上午11时20分，我在湖北路与汉口路交汇处执勤时，注意到约20名日本士兵，由一名日本警官陪同，沿汉口路福建路以西路段向东行进。因此，我清除了道路上的车辆和行人，以便让士兵穿过路口。当他们全部通过路口后，我听到两声爆炸。日本士兵立即跑向湖北路与汉口路方向，我拔出佩枪，驱散了道路上的所有行人，并跑往事发地点。到达现场后，我注意到在汉口路与福建路执勤的编号C.P.C.1506的警员前往万宗（Van Tsong）（原文不清），他在那里通过电话向捕房报告。一名便衣的特务队督察也到达了现场。随后，我将受伤的士兵和行人从车道移至人行道，交通因此中断了几分钟。
后来，捕房的人员到达现场，我于上午11时40分左右返回岗位。
在湖北路，汉口路以北约30码处，西侧人行道上，我发现了一块弹片，已移交给特别股总督察。
以上是我的真实陈述。
（签名）麦桂三。

page_data.en:
Copy of Statement of Yang Zung Sung, taken at Louza
Station on the 1.1.38.

My name is Yang Zung Sung, age 24, native of Kempo,
single, unemployed, residing unnumbered house at the
corner of Fokien and Hankow Roads.

At about 11 a.m. 1/1/38, I was standing at the North
East corner of Fokien and Hankow Roads, when I observed about
30 Japanese soldiers dressed in uniform walking West on the
South side of Hankow Road.

When the Japanese soldiers arrived at the South West
corner of Fokien and Hankow Roads, I observed two Japanese
soldiers each remove an object from under their tunic which
they threw on the road in front of them, following which I
heard two explosions.

Immediately following the explosion the Japanese
soldiers started to run West on Hankow Road turning North
on Hoopoh Road.

I did not see anything further.

The above is a true statement.
page_data.zh:
杨宗松陈述书副本，1938年1月1日于老闸捕房录供。

我叫杨宗松，24岁，金浦（Kempo）人，未婚，无业，居住在福建路与汉口路转角处无门牌号的房屋内。

1938年1月1日上午11时左右，我站在福建路与汉口路的东北角，当时我看到约30名身穿制服的日本士兵沿汉口路南侧向西行走。

当日本士兵到达福建路与汉口路的西南角时，我看到两名日本士兵各自从上衣下取出一个物体，扔在他们面前的路上，随后我听到两声爆炸。

爆炸发生后，日本士兵立即开始沿汉口路向西奔跑，并在霍普路（Hoopoh Road，即虎丘路）向北转弯。

我没有看到其他情况。

以上是一份真实的陈述。

page_data.en:
Copy of Statement of Yao Sui Ding, native of Tsungming,
taken at Louza Station on the 1/1/38.

My name is Yao Sui Ding, age 24, native of Tsungming, Single,
public ricsha coolie, residing unnumbered house, Route Rene
Delastre, French Concession.

At about 11 a.m. 1/1/38, I was plying my public
ricsha, Lic. No.1633, for hire at the South West corner of
Fokien and Hankow Roads when I observed about 40 Japanese
soldiers dressed in khaki uniform walking West on Hankow
Road.

When the soldiers were passing where I was standing
I observed one of the Japanese soldiers remove some object
from under his tunic which he threw on the road at the right of
the soldiers, following which I heard an explosion and
immediately lay down on the road.

After the explosion all the Japanese soldiers ran away
in a westerly direction on Hankow Road.

As I was running away from the scene with my ricsha
I was stopped and questioned by an unknown male Chinese as to
what had happened and whilst I was explaining to him what I
had seen a Chinese Police Constable of the S.M.P, arrived on
the scene and on hearing what I had to say he brought me to
the Police Station.

The above is a true statement.
page_data.zh:
姚水定陈述书副本，崇明人，1938年1月1日于老闸捕房录供。

我叫姚水定，24岁，崇明人，未婚，公共人力车夫，居住在法租界雷纳·德拉斯特路（Route Rene Delastre，即今淡水路）无门牌号的房屋内。

1938年1月1日上午11时左右，我正在福建路与汉口路西南角驾驶牌照号为1633的公共人力车揽客，当时我看到约40名身穿卡其色制服的日本士兵沿汉口路向西行走。

当士兵们经过我站立的地方时，我看到一名日本士兵从上衣下取出某物，将其扔在士兵右侧的路上，随后我听到一声爆炸，并立即趴在路上。

爆炸后，所有日本士兵都沿汉口路向西逃散。

当我拉着人力车逃离现场时，被一名身份不明的中国男子拦下并询问发生了什么事，正当我向他解释我所看到的情况时，一名上海公共租界工部局警务处的华籍警员到达现场，听取了我的陈述后将我带到了捕房。

以上是一份真实的陈述。

page_data.en:
Wong Zung Sung, (黄润生), C.P.C.2768.
wife.
Louss 1-1-38 Interp. Chiang.

My name is Wong Zung Sung, C.P.C.2768, attached to Loussa
Station.
At 22.30 p.m. on the 1-1-38, whilst on duty at the corner
of Kiukiang and Hupeh Roads, I heard two explosions on Hankow
Road, east of Hupeh Road. After which I saw about 20 Japanese
soldiers standing on Hankow and Hupeh Roads. Accordingly I
stopped all south bound traffic and pedestrians.
Later C.P.C.1137 arrived, then I went to inform the
station by telephone.
After the incident had been reported to the station, I
found one cartridge case outside No.265 Hupeh Road, which has
been handed over to Inspector Lieu.
This is my true statement.
(Signed) Wong Zung Sung.
page_data.zh:
黄润生，C.P.C.2768。
妻子。
老闸 1938年1月1日 翻译：Chiang。

我叫黄润生，编号C.P.C.2768，配属老闸捕房。
1938年1月1日晚上10时30分，我在九江路与湖北路转角执勤时，听到湖北路以东的汉口路传来两声爆炸。随后我看到约20名日本士兵站在汉口路与湖北路。因此，我拦截了所有南行的车辆和行人。
后来，编号C.P.C.1137的警员到达，随后我去通过电话向捕房报告。
在向捕房报告事件后，我在湖北路265号外发现了一个弹壳，已移交给刘督察。
以上是我的真实陈述。
（签名）黄润生。

page_data.en:
Hyung Ts Dong (景志堂), C.P.S. 1188.
Self.
Louza Stn. 1-1-38 Interp. Chiang.

My name is Ching Ts Dong, C.P.S. 1188 attached to Louza
Station.
At 11.25.a.m. 1-1-38, at Jukiang and Hupeh Roads corner
I encountered C.I.O. 2768, and we saw many Japanese soldiers
standing at Hankow and Hupeh Road's corner. They proceeded
South to North along Hupeh Road, turning east along Jukiang
Road.
Chief Inspector I/C and Inspector Jou came to the scene
and found a small piece of shrapnel and a cartridge case
outside 270 Hupeh Road.
This is my true statement.

Signed Hyung Ts Dong.
page_data.zh:
景志堂，C.P.S. 1188。
本人。
老闸捕房 1938年1月1日 翻译：Chiang。

我叫景志堂，编号C.P.S. 1188，配属老闸捕房。
1938年1月1日上午11时25分，在九江路与湖北路转角，我遇到了编号C.I.O. 2768的警员，我们看到许多日本士兵站在汉口路与湖北路转角。他们沿湖北路从南向北行进，然后沿九江路向东转弯。
艾克总督察（Chief Inspector I/C）和周督察（Inspector Jou）来到现场，在湖北路270号外发现了一小块弹片和一个弹壳。
以上是我的真实陈述。

签名 景志堂。

page_data.en:
Woo Hau 3z (吳侯氏), age 46,
Lou:z.    1-1-38    Intmp. Chiang.

My name is Woo Hau 3z, age 46, native of Shanghai,
S/refugee residing at the Ah Gong Leu Refugee, Camp, Canton
Road.

At about 10: a.m. 1-1-38, I, accompanied by Yung Koo 3s,
proceeded to Hoong's Church, Y... Road with the
intention to purchase cooked rice. Finding that it was too
early to start purchasing, we decided to return back. On
Hankow Road near ... Bank, I saw two explosions, and saw
about fifty or sixty brown uniformed Japanese soldiers run away
in all directions.

(Signed) Woo Hau 3z.
page_data.zh:
吴侯氏，46岁，
老闸。    1938年1月1日    翻译：Chiang。

我叫吴侯氏，46岁，上海人，难民，居住在广东路阿公乐难民收容所。

1938年1月1日上午10时左右，我与雍姑氏（Yung Koo 3s）一同前往……路洪氏教堂（Hoong's Church），打算购买熟米饭。发现开始购买的时间尚早，我们决定返回。在汉口路靠近……银行处，我看到两次爆炸，并看到约五六十名身穿棕色制服的日本士兵向四面八方逃散。

（签名）吴侯氏。

page_data.en:
Yang Kang Sung
//  .C. 348
Gaza Stn.           1-1-38

By name in Yang Kang Sung, age 24, native of Kampo,
of nationality, Korean, at a shoe shop situated at the mouth
of ... railway on Nanking Road.

At about 11.15 a.m. 1-1-38 while I was standing on the
... about 40 or
50 Japanese soldiers in full uniform walking from east to
west ... taking photos by themselves
... in second-hand
clothing shops. ... one of the Japanese
soldiers, who ... near Nanking
Road, took out a bomb in black colour
about 4 inches long ... roadway and it then
exploded. I saw another soldier take out a
similar bomb from his pocket with his right hand and hurl it
likewise
towards the centre of the road and it also exploded. Follow-
ing the explosion of the bombs the Japanese soldiers scattered
away towards Nippon Road as were a number of Chinese pedestrians.
A female Chinese and three boys were found lying on the ground
and removed to the hospital by ambulance. I was later brought
to the station by a Chinese police inspector.

The above is my true statement.

Cross-marked Yang Kang Sung
page_data.zh:
杨康成
// .C. 348
加扎捕房           1938年1月1日

我叫杨康成，24岁，金浦（Kampo）人，朝鲜籍，在南京路……铁路口的一家鞋店工作。

1938年1月1日上午11时15分左右，当我站在……时，约40或50名全副武装的日本士兵从东向西行走……自行拍照……在旧衣店里。……一名日本士兵，在……靠近南京路处，拿出一枚长约4英寸的黑色炸弹……路面，随后爆炸。我看到另一名士兵用右手从口袋里掏出一枚类似的炸弹，同样扔向路中央，随后也爆炸了。炸弹爆炸后，日本士兵向日本路（Nippon Road，即今山阴路或类似译名，此处依原文直译）方向四散奔逃，许多中国行人也是如此。发现一名中国女性和三名男孩躺在地上，由救护车送往医院。后来我被一名华籍警督带到捕房。

以上是我的真实陈述。

画十字标记 杨康成

page_data.en:
// ... Hill Ling Sung

... native of Kiangsu,
... 5130, residing at a straw
... public ricksha
... on Wenus Road
... various roads.
... without
... seeking
... I saw a group of
... soldiers in ... uniforms walking at
... the front of their
... number ... along ... road. I then intended to
... but was stopped by the Japanese
... soldiers ... and crossed ... Road. When only
... half of the ... soldiers had crossed ... Road
... observed one of them at the south-west corner of ... and
... Hankow Rd., ... with ... foot a bomb which then rolled towards
... west of the road. Having seen the bomb, I immediately turned
and proceeded south with my ricksha, but being so afraid I even-
tually discarded the vehicle. However, no sooner had the bomb
exploded than it inflicted wounds on my left leg which caused me
unable to walk but to sit on the pavement of the road. I was
later sent to the Teh Kee Hospital by ambulance and after
receiving treatment was brought to the Louza Police Station where
I found my ricksha.

The above is my true statement.
Tang Sun Sang
Commissioned & Witnessed
page_data.zh:
// …… 唐孙桑

……江苏人，
……5130，居住在稻草……
……公共人力车
……在文尼司路（Wenus Road，音译）
……各条道路。
……没有
……寻找
……我看到一群
……身穿……制服的士兵走在
……他们的
……数量……沿……路。于是我打算
……但被日本
……士兵拦住……并穿过……路。当只有
……一半的……士兵穿过……路时
……观察到其中一人在……和
……汉口路的西南角，……用脚踢了一枚炸弹，炸弹随后滚向
……路的西侧。看到炸弹后，我立即转身
拉着人力车向南走，但由于非常害怕，我最终丢弃了车辆。然而，炸弹刚一爆炸，就炸伤了我的左腿，使我无法行走，只能坐在路边的人行道上。后来我被救护车送往德济医院（Teh Kee Hospital），接受治疗后被带到老闸捕房，在那里我找到了我的人力车。

以上是我的真实陈述。
唐孙桑
委任并见证

page_data.en:
Shanghai
Louza Stn.
1-1-38
// 223

native of Shanghai, 3/female
62 Canton Road (refugee camp).

At 10.30 a.m., I proceeded to the Poor's Memorial
Branch, to do some odd jobs. As I learned that the
cooking of rice for the refugees had been completed, therefore I
went back to my refuge. On my way then passing Nankow Rd
near Yochow Rd I saw a group of persons, several tens in
number, dressed in khaki uniforms, marching from east to west along
Nankow Road. When they were about to cross Naiden Road I heard
an explosion of bomb and many people were injured. I then sat
on the pavement and was taken to the hospital by a policeman. Later
I was sent to the General Hospital.

Cross-examined.
page_data.zh:
上海
老闸捕房
1938年1月1日
// 223

上海人，3/女性
广东路62号（难民收容所）。

Sir,

I beg to state that on receipt of a report by phone from
C.P.C. 1544 at 11.25 a.m. 1-1-38 that bombs had been thrown
at a party of Japanese on Hankow Road near Fokien Road the
undersigned and C.I. Shellswell accompanied by Insp. Liu Ya
Ying proceeded by car to the scene.

On reaching Kiukiang and Hoopeh Roads intersection I
saw a party of about 25 Japanese soldiers run wildly from
Hankow Road going West and then turn North into Hoopeh Road.
Some of the soldiers had drawn bayonets in their hands and
one soldier had a pistol in his hand. This man when running
North along Hoopeh Road turned and fired a shot in the air
without taking any aim at any particular object.

Some 8 or 9 soldiers took refuge in a silk shop on the
West side of Hoopeh Road a few yards North of Hankow Road
(225 Hoopeh Road) whilst the others kept on running North
along Hoopeh Road and then turned East into Kiukiang Road.
At this time the streets in this vicinity were entirely cleared
of Chinese pedestrians.

By the time I had run as far South as the mentioned
Silk Shop a dark coloured closed motor car drove up and in the
vehicle were three men dressed in Khaki uniforms. The driver
I took to be a S.V.C. Private whilst two at the rear were
British Army Officers, one was a Lt. Colonel and the other
a Lieutenant.

The Officers asked what the trouble was and I explained
briefly what I knew.

At this time two wounded Japanese were brought over to
the car and by signs the three soldiers who were escorting

到达九江路与湖北路交叉口时，
我看见约25名日本士兵从汉口路向西疯狂奔跑，然后向北转入湖北路。
部分士兵手中拔出了刺刀，
一名士兵手中持有手枪。此人在沿湖北路向北奔跑时，转身向空中开了一枪，
并未瞄准任何特定目标。

约8或9名士兵躲进湖北路西侧、汉口路以北几码处的一家丝绸店
（湖北路225号），而其他人则继续
沿湖北路向北奔跑，随后向东转入九江路。
此时，附近街道上的中国行人已全部清空。

当我向南跑到上述
丝绸店时，一辆深色封闭式汽车驶来，
车上有三名身穿卡其色制服的男子。我认为司机是
上海志愿队（S.V.C.）的一名列兵，而后座的两人是
英国陆军军官，一人是中校，另一人
是少尉。

军官们询问发生了什么事，我简要
解释了我所知的情况。

此时，两名受伤的日本人是被带到
车旁的，通过手势，护送他们的三名士兵

VERDICT GIVEN IN BOMB
THROWER'S DEATH.
Without mentioning the deceased's
nationality, Procurator Soong of the
Settlement Chinese court gave a ver-
dict at the mortuary yesterday to
the effect that the unknown male
person, who was shot by a Chinese
police constable after he had tossed
a hand grenade at Japanese troops
passing east along Nanking Road on
December 3, had died from gunshot
wounds. Inspr. E. E. Williamson and
Sub-Inspr. J. McPhee attended on
behalf of the Louza Police Station.

page_data.en:
POLICE SEEKING
IDENTITY OF
GRENADE THROWER

In their efforts to establish the
identity of the man who threw the
home-made grenade at parading
Japanese soldiers on Nanking Road
last Friday, wounding four Japanese
and one foreign police officer, the
Shanghai Municipal Police, who are
now in charge of the case, have cir-
cularised the Chinese press.

A death picture of the man's face
is printed with the request that re-
latives of the man come forward
and claim the body which is still
being held at the temporary public
mortuary on Kiaochow Road.

Until the identity of the man and
his nationality have been definitely
established by relatives or friends,
the police will have little informa-
tion on which they can work in
their efforts to learn the motive
for the man's act.

An inquest over the remains of
the bomb-tosser was held at the
Kiaochow Road mortuary yesterday
morning.

No verdict was reached in regard
to his nationality but the decision
was made that the Settlement
police authorities continue their
efforts to establish the fellow's
identity.

The autopsy which was scheduled
to take place at the Country Hos-
pital Tuesday afternoon over the
body of the man, said in some
quarters to be a Korean, but de-
clared by the Japanese to be a
Chinese, was called off at the last
moment when the Japanese authori-
ties decided that it was unnecessary.

Following the inquest yesterday, it
was decided to turn the body over
to the Shanghai Public Benevolent
Cemetery in a few days for burial
provided no one turns up to claim
it in the meantime.

昨日上午，在胶州路停尸房

关于其国籍未达成裁决，但决定

确认此人的身份。

page_data.en:
Alleged
Japanese
Demands

Four Provisions Stated
In Note; Independent
Action Is Wanted

It was ascertained here yesterday from usually reliable sources that the demands presented to the Shanghai Municipal Council by the Japanese on Friday night a few hours after the Nanking Road incident included four provisions.

The Japanese wish to have it understood that armed forces can pass through the Settlement at any time without advance notice to the Council. The Council is likewise urged to take energetic steps to prevent a recurrence of the incident, and, if necessary, the Japanese insist that they have a right to take independent and effective measures. Finally the Japanese wish to have permission to examine suspects inside the Settlement and take other steps, according to this report.

No official confirmation regarding these demands was available here yesterday, but in well-informed circles it was emphatically stated that such provisions were contained in a note handed to the Council by the Japanese on Friday.

The Council's attitude in the matter was expressed in a statement which has already been published, this being to the effect that the Commissioner of Police had entered into no agreement with the Japanese on Friday night.
page_data.zh:
据称
日本
提出的要求

照会中列出四项条款；
要求采取独立行动

据本地通常可靠的消息来源昨日获悉，日本方面在周五晚间，即南京路事件发生几小时后，向上海公共租界工部局提出的要求包括四项条款。

日本方面希望明确，武装部队可以随时通过租界，无需事先通知工部局。同时敦促工部局采取有力措施防止此类事件再次发生，如有必要，日本方面坚持认为他们有权采取独立且有效的措施。最后，据该报告称，日本方面希望获准在租界内审查嫌疑人并采取其他步骤。

昨日此处无法获得关于这些要求的官方确认，但在消息灵通人士中坚决表示，周五日本方面递交给工部局的照会中包含了此类条款。

工部局对此事的态度已在已发表的声明中表达，大意是警务处处长在周五晚间未与日本方面达成任何协议。

page_data.en:
The announced movement of about 6,000 Japanese
infantry, artillery, and auxiliary troops from Jess-
field to Hongkew through the Settlement began at
shortly after 1100 yesterday. The column consisted
of three battalions of infantry, two battalions (6
batteries, 24 guns) of light artillery (75 mm), a
company of engineers and miscellaneous auxiliaries
including a few cavalry. The units were of a reservist
division. The men appeared in excellent physical con-
dition, guns and equipment in fair shape, although
obviously having seen hard service. Animals were in
very poor condition apparently underfed and not well
cared for. The march proceeded without serious incident
until about 1245 when the rear portion of the column was
passing Nanking and Kiangsi Roads. At this point a
grenade-bomb (described as similar to the Mills grenade)
was thrown over the column. Upon bursting, it in-
jured three Japanese soldiers, a Japanese Consular
Policeman, and three members of the Shanghai Municipal
Police. The assassin was shot on the spot by a Chin-
ese constable of the S.M.P., and died about two hours
later. The section of the parade, which was disrupted
by the explosion, was promptly reassembled, and march-
ed on, leaving a detail behind to clear and patrol the
area. Patrols spread out on Nanking and adjacent roads,
reaching as far east as Shansi Road, and as far as
Tientsin, Kiukiang and Yu Ya Ching Roads on the
north, south, and west. At about 1525 the Jap-
anese troops extended their patrols into the Ameri-
can sector west of Yu Ya Ching Road. They placed
portable barbed-wire barricades across Bubbling
Well Road just to the west of the Grand Theater and
stationed an officer and two sentries at this point,
stopping all traffic. Upon being informed of the
violation of the American sector by Colonel Price,
the Japanese officer in command of the detail caused
it to be withdrawn east of Yu Ya Ching Road.

A joint investigation of the bombing was held
by the Municipal Police and the Japanese. At about
2000, the investigation completed, the Japanese
patrols began to withdraw, and at 2030, the area
was entirely open.
page_data.zh:
昨日11时过后不久，约6000名日本步兵、炮兵及辅助部队从极司菲尔（Jessfield）经公共租界向虹口进发的既定行动开始。该纵队由三个步兵营、两个轻炮兵营（6个连，24门75毫米火炮）、一个工兵连以及包括少量骑兵在内的各类辅助人员组成。这些部队隶属于一个后备师团。士兵们身体状况极佳，枪炮和装备虽显陈旧，显然经历过艰苦服役，但尚属良好。牲畜状况极差，明显喂养不足且照料不周。行军过程未发生重大事故，直到约12时45分，当纵队后部经过南京路和江西路时，一枚手榴弹（据描述类似于米尔斯手榴弹）被投掷到纵队上方。爆炸造成三名日本士兵、一名日本领事警察以及三名上海公共租界工部局警务处警员受伤。刺客被一名华籍巡捕当场击毙，约两小时后死亡。受爆炸干扰的行进队伍迅速重新集结并继续前进，留下一支分队负责清理和巡逻该区域。巡逻队扩散至南京路及周边道路，东抵山西路，北、南、西分别延伸至天津路、九江路和虞洽卿路。约15时25分，日军将巡逻范围扩展至虞洽卿路以西的美方辖区。他们在静安寺路大光明大戏院西侧设置便携式铁丝网路障，并在此部署一名军官和两名哨兵，阻断所有交通。普莱斯上校（Colonel Price）告知日军此举侵犯了美方辖区后，负责该分队的日军军官遂令其撤至虞洽卿路以东。

工部局警务处与日方对爆炸事件进行了联合调查。约20时，调查结束，日军巡逻队开始撤离，至20时30分，该区域完全恢复开放。

page_data.en:
NANKING ROAD INCIDENT

THE Nanking Road Incident of Friday has happily been closed, and the strained atmosphere has found further relief in the decision by the Japanese military to call off the second parade scheduled for yesterday.

The Incident was indeed much to be regretted. As pointed out in this journal on numerous occasions, the peace and order in this international community sorely depends upon the friendly collaboration among all nationals. Any action which is likely to disturb or threaten local tranquility may be well avoided, so that the unenviable position in which the two foreign Municipal Councils have been placed may not be rendered the more complicated.

From all reports it seems that the Japanese and municipal authorities in handling the ugly situation on Friday displayed infinite restraint and tact, except perhaps for the first few moments of excitement. Shanghai may be thankful for the prompt liquidation of the affair.

It may be pertinent to point out that the Incident might have been intended by malcontents to create a panic for the purpose of fishing in troubled waters. This point may be well borne in mind by the competent authorities on future occasions.
page_data.zh:
南京路事件

上周五的南京路事件已幸告平息，随着日军决定取消原定于昨日举行的第二次阅兵，紧张气氛得到进一步缓解。

此次事件确实令人遗憾。正如本刊多次指出的那样，这个国际社区的和平与秩序严重依赖于各国侨民之间的友好合作。任何可能扰乱或威胁当地安宁的行动都应尽量避免，以免使两个外国工部局所处的尴尬处境变得更加复杂。

从各方报告来看，除了最初片刻的激动情绪外，日本当局和工部局当局在处理周五的恶劣局势时表现出了极大的克制和策略。上海应当庆幸此事得以迅速解决。

值得指出的是，不满分子可能意图制造恐慌，以便浑水摸鱼。主管当局在今后的类似场合中应充分铭记这一点。

page_data.en:
S. M. C. Issues Statement
On Nanking Road Incident

In a statement issued yesterday afternoon, the Shanghai Municipal
Council made clear its position in regard to the Nanking Road affair
of Friday afternoon in which four Japanese and one foreign police
officer were wounded when a bomb was thrown by a youth said to
have been a Chinese. The Council's statement follows:
"In order that there may be no misunderstanding of the position,
the Shanghai Municipal Council desires it to be known that no agree-
ment was entered into on the night of December 3 between the
Commissioner of Police and Japanese military representatives.
"A document was drawn up by the Japanese Commander-in-Chief's
representative in a conversation which he had with the Commissioner
of Police before the withdrawal of Japanese troops from Nanking Road.
"The Commissioner of Police emphasised that he had no authority
to enter into any agreement, and in order to make it clear that the
document in question did not purport to be an agreement he endorsed
it to the effect that he had read and understood the document and
would bring its contents to the notice of the Council.
"The Commissioner of Police also emphasised that he could make
no agreement with regard to the passage of Japanese troops through
the International Settlement.
"The Shanghai Municipal Council also desires it to be known that
the Council's representatives had, previously to the parade of Japanese
troops through the Settlement, stressed to the Japanese authorities the
inadvisability of holding such a parade at the present time.
"The Shanghai Municipal Council has made a full report to the
Senior Consul of the occurrences which took place on Friday, December
3."
page_data.zh:
工部局就南京路事件发表声明

工部局于昨日下午发表声明，阐明了其关于周五下午南京路事件的立场。在该事件中，一名据称为中国人的青年投掷炸弹，导致四名日本人和一名外籍警官受伤。工部局声明如下：
“为避免对立场产生误解，上海公共租界工部局希望公众知悉，警务处处长与日本军方代表在12月3日晚并未达成任何协议。
“在日本军队从南京路撤离之前，日军司令官代表在与警务处处长的谈话中起草了一份文件。
“警务处处长强调，他无权签署任何协议，并且为了明确该文件并非协议，他在文件上批注，表示已阅读并理解该文件内容，并将把其内容提请工部局注意。
“警务处处长还强调，他不能就日军通过公共租界事宜达成任何协议。
“上海公共租界工部局还希望公众知悉，在日军通过租界阅兵之前，工部局代表已向日本当局强调，目前举行此类阅兵是不明智的。
“上海公共租界工部局已向首席领事全面报告了12月3日（星期五）发生的事件。”

page_data.en:
JAPANESE APPRECIATE
PRECAUTIONS TAKEN
BY TWO CONCESSIONS

Appreciation of the steps taken by the authorities of the French Concession and the International Settlement in patrolling the streets traversed on Friday by the Japanese military forces in their parade from the Jessfield area to Hongkew was expressed on behalf of the Japanese high command by a military spokesman at the press conference yesterday morning.

"As you all know, a deplorable incident occurred in the course of the march," he said. "The affair, however, is now regarded as closed, the Shanghai Municipal Police having agreed to prevent, to the best of their ability, the recurrence of such incidents, following an exchange of views between representatives of the Japanese army and the police."

Said To Be Chinese

Answering questions, the spokesman stated that contrary to previous reports, the man who threw the hand grenade at the passing Japanese troops near the Sun Sun Department Store building on Nanking Road at 12.50 p.m. Friday, is now definitely known to have been a Chinese. It also has been ascertained that the "bomb" was a home-made affair.

The man was given medical attention after being shot by a Chinese Police Constable of the S.M.P., first by a Chinese physician summoned by the S.M.P. and later by a Japanese doctor who appeared on the scene.

He was not removed from the Kwangse Road pavement where he was taken after being shot down by the Chinese constable. He lived for some time after the shooting and died on the pavement. The body is now reported to be in the hands of the Shanghai Municipal Police authorities.

The three wounded Japanese soldiers were reported to be in fair condition yesterday. Their wounds are not regarded as serious. The Japanese Consular Police officer who was wounded during the explosion, is reported to be seriously wounded about the hips and his recovery is now expected to take some time. The wounds of Inspector John McPhee, of the S.M.P., who was struck in a leg and an arm, are not now regarded as serious.

No Shot Fired

Early reports circulated Friday to the effect that a shot had been fired from the fourth floor of the Sun Sun Company's hotel on the Kwangse Road side of the building shortly after the bombing, were declared to be false by the management of the hotel.

It is now reported that a Nipponese soldier standing at the corner of Kwangse and Nanking Roads fired a shot and that the puff of smoke observers saw floating out of the window was plaster knocked loose by the bullet.

In the meantime, the Shanghai Municipal Police authorities are carrying on with their investigation of the bombing incident.
page_data.zh:
日方赞赏两租界采取的预防措施

昨日早晨的新闻发布会上，一位军事发言人代表日军高层，对法租界和公共租界当局在周五日军从极司菲尔地区向虹口阅兵途中所经街道进行巡逻的措施表示赞赏。

他说：“众所周知，行军过程中发生了一起不幸事件。然而，此事现被视为已结案，继日军代表与警方交换意见后，上海公共租界工部局警务处已同意尽其所能防止此类事件再次发生。”

据称为中国人

在回答提问时，该发言人称，与此前报道相反，周五中午12时50分在南京路先施公司大楼附近向行进中的日军投掷手榴弹的人，现已确认为中国人。此外已查明，该“炸弹”系自制物品。

该男子被工部局警务处的一名华籍巡捕击伤后，先由工部局警务处召来的中国医生进行救治，随后由赶到现场的日本医生进行治疗。

他被击倒后并未从广西路人行道上移走。他在中枪后存活了一段时间，最终死在人行道上。据报道，其遗体现由上海公共租界工部局警务处当局保管。

据报道，三名受伤的日本士兵昨日状况良好。他们的伤势不被认为严重。在爆炸中受伤的日本领事警察官员，据报道臀部重伤，预计需要一段时间才能康复。工部局警务处督察约翰·麦克菲（John McPhee）腿部和手臂受伤，目前其伤势也不被认为严重。

未开枪

周五早期流传的报告称，爆炸发生后不久，有人从广西路一侧的先施公司旅馆四楼开了一枪，酒店管理层宣称此说法不实。

现有报道称，是一名日本士兵在广西路与南京路路口开了一枪，观察者看到的从窗户飘出的烟雾其实是子弹击落的灰泥粉尘。

与此同时，上海公共租界工部局警务处当局正在继续对爆炸事件进行调查。

page_data.en:
Japanese Daily Says
S.M.P. "Insincere"

Severely criticizing the "inade-
quacy" of measures taken by the
Shanghai Municipal Police to
maintain peace during last Friday's
march of the Japanese troops
through the Settlement, the Shang-
hai United News, a Japanese daily,
yesterday declared the S. M. P. had
displayed "A lukewarm and insin-
cere" attitude in suppressing the
anti-Nipponese movement.

The failure of the S. M. P. to
take all necessary steps had re-
sulted in injuries to four Japanese,
the daily pointed out.

"In fact," the journal said, "the
only step taken by the S. M. P.
to curb anti-Japanese terrorism
has been to shoot the man respon-
sible for the Nanking Road in-
cident."

This, the Japanese newspaper as-
serted, "shows that the Municipa'
Police is incapable of keeping the
anti-Japanese movement and ter-
rorism in check."

The daily further expressed
regret at the alleged insult to the
Japanese flag by a Briton on
Nanking Road.

The parade, the journal asserted,
was "not unusual," since the
British troops had marched across
the Settlements during the tense
days of 1927, when the anti-
British sentiment in China was at
its height.

The only bright spot in the day's
proceedings, according to the daily,
was the "joy displayed by Japanese
subjects in greeting the marching
Japanese troops."
page_data.zh:
日本日报称工部局警务处“不真诚”

日本日报《上海联合新闻》（Shanghai United News）昨日严厉批评上海公共租界工部局警务处在上周五日军通过租界行军期间维持和平的措施“不力”，宣称工部局警务处在镇压反日运动方面表现出“冷淡且不真诚”的态度。

该报指出，工部局警务处未能采取一切必要步骤，导致四名日本人受伤。

该报称：“事实上，工部局警务处为遏制反日恐怖主义所采取的唯一措施，就是枪击了应对南京路事件负责的那个人。”

这家日本报纸断言，这“表明工部局警务处无力控制反日运动和恐怖主义”。

该报还对据称一名英国人在南京路侮辱日本国旗一事表示遗憾。

该报断言，这次阅兵“并不罕见”，因为在1927年那些紧张的日子里，当中国的反英情绪达到顶峰时，英国军队也曾穿过租界。

据该报称，当天活动中唯一的亮点是“日本侨民在欢迎行进中的日军时所表现出的喜悦”。

page_data.en:
Official Statement By
Council Denies Making
Agreement With Japanese

SEQUEL TO REPORTS THAT COMMISSIONER
HAD AGREED TO LIST OF DEMANDS ON
FRIDAY, FOLLOWING BOMB INCIDENT

ENDORSED DOCUMENT THAT HE WOULD
TELL COUNCIL OF CONTENTS

Overseas Comment Is Critical That Parade Was
Ever Staged; Military Spokesmen Expresses
Appreciation Of Protective Measures

In consequence of reports that Major F. W. Gerrard, Com-
missioner of Police, had entered into an agreement with the
Japanese military authorities on Friday evening, prior to the
withdrawal of Japanese military units from the Central District,
following the throwing of a bomb during the march of Japanese
troops through the city, the Shanghai Municipal Council caused
the following official statement to be issued last evening:—

“In order that there may be no
misunderstanding of the position,
the Shanghai Municipal Council de-
sires it to be known that no agree-
ment was entered into on the night
of December 3 between the Com-
missioner of Police and Japanese
military representatives.

“A document was drawn up by
Japanese officers setting out the
points made by the Japanese Com-
mander-in-Chief’s representative in
a conversation which he had with
the Commissioner of Police before
the withdrawal of Japanese troops
from Nanking Road.

“The Commissioner of Police em-
phasized that he had no authority
to enter into any agreement, and in
order to make it clear that the
document in question did not purport
to be an agreement he endorsed it
to the effect that he had read and
understood the document and would
bring its contents to the notice of
the Council. The Commissioner of
Police also emphasized that he
could make no agreement with re-
gard to the passage of Japanese
troops through the International
Settlement.

“The Shanghai Municipal Council
also desires it to be known that the
Council’s representatives had, pre-
viously to the parade of Japanese
troops through the Settlement,
stressed to the Japanese authorities
the inadvisability of holding such a
parade at the present time.

“The Shanghai Municipal Council
has made a full report to the Senior
Consul of the occurrences which
took place on Friday, December 3.”

Earlier Reports
According to earlier reports,
four demands were made by Japan-
ese authorities in a statement pres-
ented on Friday night to the Com-
missioner of Police, all the cir-
cumstances of the investigation made by
police and Japanese military re-
presentatives.

In presenting the demands, the
reports stated, Colonel [illegible],
acting for General [illegible], stressed
the right of Japanese troops to
pass through the Settlement at any
time, and demanded that the police
should take steps to prevent a re-
currence of incidents such as the
bombing which took place during
the march of Japanese troops
through Shanghai on Friday.

That if the Japanese army regards
the steps taken by the Shanghai
Municipal Police as inadequate, it
reserves the right to take whatever
steps it deems necessary to preserve
the peace of the Settlement; and

That the Japanese army, regard-
ing the Shanghai Municipal Police
as incapable of effectively prevent-
ing anti-Japanism in the Settlement,
reserves the right to take any neces-
sary steps, including the examina-
tion of persons and the searching
of property.

Appreciates Measures
Appreciation of the steps taken
by the authorities of the French
Concession and the International
Settlement in patrolling the streets
traversed on Friday by the Japanese
military forces in their march from
the Jessfield area to Hongkew was
expressed on behalf of the Japanese
high command by a military spokes-
man at yesterday’s press conference.

“As you all know, a deplorable in-
cident occurred in the course of the
march,” he continued. The affair,
however, is now regarded as closed,
the Shanghai Municipal Police hav-
ing agreed to prevent, to the best
of their ability, the recurrence of
such incidents, following an ex-
change of views between representa-
tives of the Japanese Army and the
police.”

Strong British Comment
LONDON, Dec. 4.—“It was a
wholly unnecessary march of pro-
vocation,” declares the “Daily
Telegraph” in commenting on the
Japanese parade yesterday through
the International Settlement in
Shanghai, which is the subject of
much comment in several morn-
ing papers. Referring to the bomb
incident, the paper says: “The
Japanese authorities have every
right to be angry about the bomb
incident, but they had no right to
make a triumphal procession
through the International Settle-
ment. It was a piece of sheer bra-
vado, and it has done nothing to
improve the situation.”

anese parade. Indeed, it may be
questioned whether, perhaps, the
parade did not take place in the
hope that the ‘incident’ would be
bigger; for this was no march of
triumph through a conquered ter-
ritory, as it was not with the In-
ternational Settlement that Japan
has been waging her undeclared
war.

“Times” Is Critical
Under the heading of “Vainglory
of Shanghai,” the “Times” introdu-
ces its comment on the parade with
the remark that “Japan periodic-
ally, and often in a curiously
ostentatious manner, parades her
most serious weakness before the
world. That weakness, implicit in
the limitations of the Japanese
military mind and its workings,
was seen yesterday in a character-
istic light.”

“At best,” the “Times” declares,
yesterday’s parade would have
been an artless piece of pomp....
Seen in its true perspective it was
a typical product of Japan’s zeal
and Japan’s nerve, and is import-
ant only as reflecting the attitude
of Japan’s Army towards all for-
eign rights in China.

“The Shanghai Municipal Coun-
cil may well feel relieved that
nothing more occurred,” the
“Times” concludes.

Liberal Journal Views
“The Japanese were trailing their
coats,” says the “News-Chronicle.”
“What they hoped to gain by that
is not clear.”

Japan’s behaviour, it says, has
sorely tried the International Set-
tlement in Shanghai, and the police
have been remarkable.

“So wanton,” declares the Man-
chester “Guardian” “was the
Japanese decision to march through
the International Settlement, that
it is hard to avoid the suspicion
that they hoped to create an ex-
cuse to strengthen their grip on
the Settlement. Yet, if this fully
proved anything, it was the cap-
ability of the Settlement authorities
to maintain order unaided (though
not unhindered).”—Reuter.

Lively Apprehension
LONDON, Dec. 4.—The bomb in-
cident, which occurred during the
Japanese parade through the Inter-
national Settlement in Shanghai yes-
terday, has excited lively apprehen-
sions regarding Japan’s action as a
result.

Referring to the Japanese protest
against anti-Japanese activities in
Hongkong, the “News-Chronicle”
says that “it is almost inconceivable
that a Conservative Government
can stomach a direct attack on the
Union Jack or an attempt to dictate
policies in any territory over which
the Union Jack flies.”—Reuter.

French Press Reactions
PARIS, Dec. 4.—The incidents
which occurred during the Japanese
military parade in Shanghai are pro-
minently featured by the press here
and the general impression is that
the affair will have serious conse-
quences.
page_data.zh:
工部局官方声明
否认与日方达成协议

继周五炸弹事件后，有报道称警务处长已同意一份要求清单

他签注文件称将向工部局通报其内容

海外舆论批评游行根本不应举行；军方发言人感谢保护措施

鉴于有报告称，在日军穿越市区行进期间发生投掷炸弹事件后，警务处处长 F. W. Gerrard 少校于周五晚间、日军部队撤离中区之前，与日本军方当局达成了一项协议，上海公共租界工部局遂于昨晚发布如下官方声明：—

“为免对局势产生任何误解，
上海公共租界工部局希望公众知悉，12月3日晚，警务处处长与日本军方代表之间并未达成任何协议。

“一份文件由日本军官起草，列明了日本总司令代表在与警务处处长就日军从南京路撤军一事进行交谈时所提出的要点。

“警务处处长强调，他无权达成任何协议，并且为明确该文件并非旨在构成一项协议，他在文件上签注，表明其已阅读并理解该文件，并将把其内容提请工部局注意。警务处处长还强调，他就日军通过国际公共租界一事，无法达成任何协议。

“上海公共租界工部局亦希望公众知悉，在日军部队通过租界游行之前，工部局代表已向日本当局强调，目前举行此类游行是不明智的。

“上海公共租界工部局已就12月3日（星期五）发生的事件，向首席领事提交了完整报告。”

早期报道
据早期报道，日本当局在周五晚间向警务处处长提交的一份声明中提出了四项要求，这些要求均基于警方和日本军方代表所进行的调查情况。

报道指出，在提出这些要求时，代表 [原文不清] 将军行事的 [原文不清] 上校强调了日军随时通过租界的权利，并要求警方采取措施，防止类似周五日军穿越上海行进期间发生的炸弹袭击等事件再次发生。

如果日本军队认为上海公共租界警务处采取的措施不足，它保留采取其认为必要的任何措施以维护租界和平的权利；以及

日本军队认为上海公共租界警务处无力有效防止租界内的反日情绪，因此保留采取任何必要步骤的权利，包括检查人员和搜查财产。

感谢措施
在昨日的新闻发布会上，一位军方发言人代表日本最高指挥部，对法租界和国际公共租界当局在周五日军从极司菲尔（Jessfield）地区行进至虹口途中所经过街道的巡逻工作表示感谢。

“众所周知，在行进过程中发生了一起令人遗憾的事件，”他继续说道。“然而，此事现在被视为已了结，因为在日本陆军代表与警方交换意见后，上海公共租界警务处已同意尽其所能防止此类事件再次发生。”

英国舆论强烈批评
伦敦，12月4日电。——《每日电讯报》在评论昨日日军在上海国际公共租界的游行时宣称：“这是一次完全不必要的挑衅性游行。”该报是多家晨报中对此事发表评论的报纸之一。提及炸弹事件时，该报称：“日本当局完全有理由对炸弹事件感到愤怒，但他们无权在国际公共租界举行凯旋游行。这纯粹是一种虚张声势的行为，无助于改善局势。”

确实，人们不禁要问，这次游行的举行，或许正是希望‘事件’闹得更大；因为这并非穿过被征服领土的胜利进军，因为日本进行的未宣战战争的对象并非国际公共租界。

《泰晤士报》持批评态度
《泰晤士报》以“上海的虚荣”为题，在评论游行时开篇指出：“日本定期地、且常以一种奇特的炫耀方式，向世界展示其最严重的弱点。这种弱点隐含在日本军事思维及其运作的局限性之中，在昨天的事件中得到了典型的体现。”

《泰晤士报》宣称，“退一步说，昨日的游行也不过是一场朴素的炫耀……若从正确的角度来看，它是日本狂热与日本胆量的典型产物，其重要性仅在于反映了日本陆军对中国所有外国权利的态度。”

《泰晤士报》总结道：“上海公共租界工部局大可以因未发生更多事端而感到宽慰。”

自由派报刊观点
《新闻纪事报》称：“日本人是在故意挑衅。他们希望从中获得什么尚不清楚。”

该报称，日本的行径严重考验了上海国际公共租界，而警方的表现值得称赞。

曼彻斯特《卫报》宣称：“日本决定穿越国际公共租界行进的举动如此肆意妄为，以至于人们很难不怀疑他们希望制造借口以加强对租界的控制。然而，如果这充分证明了什么，那就是证明租界当局有能力在无人协助（尽管并非毫无阻碍）的情况下维持秩序。”——路透社。

深切担忧
伦敦，12月4日电。——昨日日军在上海国际公共租界游行期间发生的炸弹事件，引发了人们对日本随后行动的深切担忧。

《新闻纪事报》在提及日本抗议香港反日活动一事时称：“保守党政府几乎不可能容忍对米字旗的直接攻击，或试图在任何飘扬着米字旗的领土上发号施令。”——路透社。

法国媒体反应
巴黎，12月4日电。——此处媒体显著报道了上海日军军事游行期间发生的事件，普遍印象是此事将产生严重后果。

Prior Action By America
WASHINGTON, Dec. 4.—Mr.
Cordell Hull, Secretary of State, re-
vealed to-day that American diplo-
matic and consular officials both in
Shanghai and Tokyo had tried to
persuade the Japanese authorities to
prevent the “victory” march of
Japanese troops through the Inter-
national Settlement at Shanghai yes-
terday.—Reuter’s American Service.

Prudence Expected
WASHINGTON, Dec. 4.—News-
papers throughout the country re-
produced under large headlines des-
patches concerning the incident in
Shanghai, and particularly the situa-
tion which occurred when Nippon-
ese troops pushed two blocks into
the American Defence Sector of the
International Settlement.
Reports received by the State De-
partment indicate that the Japanese
do not intend to exploit the incident
which occurred during the course of
their parade in order to impose new
demands upon the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council and indications con-
firm the impression current in
American diplomatic circles that
Japan will act with great prudence
in order to avoid friction with the
European powers and the United
States.—Havas.
