美国此前的行动
华盛顿，12月4日电。——国务卿科德尔·赫尔（Cordell Hull）今日透露，驻上海和东京的美国外交及领事官员曾试图说服日本当局，阻止昨日日军在上海国际公共租界举行的“胜利”游行。——路透社美国分社。

预期会谨慎行事
华盛顿，12月4日电。——全国各地的报纸均以大字标题刊登了有关上海事件的电讯，特别是当日军部队推进至国际公共租界美方防区两个街区时所发生的情况。
国务院收到的报告表明，日本无意利用游行期间发生的事件向上海公共租界工部局施加新的要求，各项迹象证实了美国外交界目前的印象，即日本将极为谨慎地行事，以避免与欧洲列强及美国发生摩擦。——哈瓦斯社。

page_data.en:
JAPANESE SEIZE S.M.C. AREA,
LATER WITHDRAW

Temporary “Military Zone” Created After Bombing
of “Victory Parade” in Nanking Road

THROWER KILLED BY CHINESE CONSTABLE

SHANGHAI was thrown into a state of extreme tension yesterday afternoon when Japanese troops occupied a large area of the International Settlement centring about the intersection of Nanking and Kwangse Roads where a bomb was exploded by an unidentified Oriental amidst the Japanese soldiers marching in a “victory parade” from Jessfield to Hongkew. The bombing occurred at 12.44 noon, wounding three Japanese soldiers, one Japanese civilian, one foreign policeman, one Sikh constable and one Chinese constable. Another Chinese constable shot and fatally wounded the bomb-thrower, while a Japanese soldier fired one rifle shot at a third-storey window of the Sun Sun Department Store without striking anybody.

The Japanese military did not permit the bomb-thrower to be removed to hospital and he later expired where he had fallen to the footpath in Kwangse Road, a short distance south of Nanking Road, with four pistol wounds in his body. He had not been identified at a late hour last night, when the Settlement Police and Japanese officers were still working on the case. The Japanese investigators insisted he was Chinese.

Many minor brushes occurred between foreigners and Japanese during the three hours of the parade and afterwards when the Japanese using, amongst others, machine-gun units and mounted men, started to make a “military zone” in the Settlement on a steadily growing scale.

The Settlement and French Police, fully mobilised for the occasion, ably dealt with one of the most delicate situations in the history of Shanghai, and along the entire route—Yu Yaan Road, Avenue Haig, Avenue Foch, Yu Ya Ching Road, Nanking Road and The Bund—the traffic problem was admirably handled.

Japanese Assurance Given

Yesterday afternoon it was understood that the Japanese authorities had expressed their satisfaction with the arrangements made by the Council’s Police for dealing with the parade. Mr. Shimazono, Japanese Consul-General, informally told the Secretary-General that the Japanese troops which had temporarily taken up a position in certain parts of the Central District would be withdrawn. A similar assurance was given to Major-General A. P. D. Turner-Smith by Major-General Sasaki.

The Japanese troops did withdraw and by 4.30 p.m. the Louza, Sincere and Chekiang Road districts were clear of them. At 5.45 Mr. S. W. Jones, Assistant Commissioner of the Settlement Police, was able to report that the Shanghai Electric Construction Company had their trams running again on Nanking Road and that traffic had resumed.

An hour later this “zone” was extended across Yu Ya Ching Road, on both sides of Bubbling Well Road, the Japanese soldiers in part using the Settlement’s barbed-wire entanglements for their own purposes. The Japanese continued as far as Myburgh and Mohawk Roads on the west and almost reached Avenue Foch to the south. Strong representations made by Col. Charles F. B. Price, commanding the Fourth United States Marines into whose sector the Japanese had penetrated, however, resulted in the speedy withdrawal of the Japanese west of Yu Ya Ching Road. Simultaneously Maj. F. W. Gerrard, Commissioner of the Settlement Police, started negotiating with the Japanese in regard to the occupation of Louza District and the area was finally cleared, permitting the resumption of traffic on Nanking Road and the return of the Chinese who had been cooped up in the Nanking Road department stores since the bombing. Armed Sikhs who were accompanied by the Japanese military patrols also did pickets of the various blocks, who attempted to stop the pedestrians from entering the area. They were unsuccessful, however, and the crowds soon returned.

Bomb-Thrower Appears

The bombing incident developed with extreme swiftness. Chinese crowds were being kept well back from Nanking Road on both sides of the military route. Suddenly, in Kwangse Road south of Nanking Road, a man dressed in a “Sun Yat Sen suit” stepped forward from the mass of onlookers and walked a few steps in the direction of Nanking Road. As a Chinese constable attempted to push him back into the crowd he produced something wrapped in a Chinese newspaper and threw it at the column of marching soldiers. It landed near the footpath on the opposite side—and exploded. It was a crudely made hand-grenade of the Mills type and it wounded three of the Japanese soldiers, a Japanese civilian, a Sikh constable, a Chinese constable, and Detective Sub-Insp. J. McPhee of Louza Station, who was also on duty at the corner. Mr. McPhee’s overcoat was torn by fragments of the bomb and one of the pieces was stopped by a bus pass he carried in an inside pocket. He suffered a flesh wound in one arm.

Before the bomb had even exploded a Chinese constable, acting clearly in accordance with instructions, promptly drew his revolver and shot the assailant—a disciplined alertness which was most impressive. Four shots were fired, each making a hit.

Consternation was caused in the ranks of the Japanese soldiers and the “banzais” of the Japanese spectators stopped suddenly. Commands were shouted and the district was quickly surrounded. Sentries were posted in all the side streets, while groups of soldiers began to search alleyways and buildings. A Japanese soldier fired a rifle shot at a window in the Sun Sun Building at about 1 o’clock, but hit the wall instead. The shot added to the confusion and sent many civilians scurrying for shelter. Ten minutes later the parade was resumed.

It was noticeable both before and after the incident how the men in the moving columns looked up at the buildings between which they were passing as if they expected trouble.

Procession Starts

Shortly before 11 a.m., the blare of bugles sounding a marching tune could be heard by the crowd of Japanese and foreigners who were waiting for the procession just inside the British defence sector, on the Bubbling Well Road Railway Crossing. Then the foremost units in the procession came into view, and halted on the other side of the railway crossing. Meanwhile, a darkly-uniformed Korean in khaki uniform passed around waving a Japanese flag, shaking hands enthusiastically with the little group of Japanese officials who had come down the street in advance of the main body. Soldiers of “Sunset” Wave guard from many points at the party of Japanese officials.
page_data.zh:
日军占领工部局辖区，
随后撤离

南京路“胜利游行”遭炸弹袭击后
设立临时“军事区”

投弹者被华捕击毙

昨日下午，当日军占领了以南京路与广西路交汇处为中心的国际公共租界大片区域时，上海陷入极度紧张状态。此前，一名身份不明的东方人在从兆丰公园（Jessfield）行进至虹口（Hongkew）的日军“胜利游行”队伍中引爆了一枚炸弹。爆炸发生于中午12时44分，造成三名日本士兵、一名日本平民、一名外籍巡捕、一名锡克教巡捕和一名华捕受伤。另一名华捕开枪击中投弹者并致其重伤，而一名日本士兵向新新百货公司三楼窗户开了一枪，未击中任何人。

日军不允许将投弹者送往医院，他后来死于广西路人行道上，该地位于南京路以南不远处，身中四枪。直至昨晚深夜，此人身份仍未查明，当时租界警务处与日本军官仍在处理此案。日本调查人员坚称其为中国人。

在游行的三小时内及之后，外侨与日军之间发生了多起小规模冲突。此后，日军动用包括机枪部队和骑兵在内的力量，开始在租界内逐步扩大建立“军事区”。

租界警务处与法租界警务处为此全面动员，妥善应对了上海历史上最为棘手的局势之一。在整个游行路线——愚园路、海格路（Avenue Haig）、福煦路（Avenue Foch）、虞洽卿路、南京路及外滩——交通问题得到了极佳的处理。

日方作出保证

昨日下午获悉，日本当局对工部局警务处为应对游行所作的安排表示满意。日本总领事岛园（Shimazono，音译）非正式地告知总办，暂时占据中区某些部位的日军部队将会撤离。佐佐木（Sasaki，音译）少将也向特纳-史密斯（A. P. D. Turner-Smith）少将作出了类似的保证。

日军确实进行了撤离，至下午4时30分，老闸、先施公司及浙江路地区已无日军踪迹。下午5时45分，租界警务处副总监琼斯（S. W. Jones）先生报告称，上海电力建设公司的电车已在南京路恢复运行，交通也已恢复。

一小时后，这一“区域”扩展至虞洽卿路对面，以及静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）两侧，部分日军甚至利用租界的铁丝网障碍物为己所用。日军向西继续推进至迈尔巴赫路（Myburgh Road，音译）和莫霍克路（Mohawk Road，音译），向南几乎抵达福煦路。然而，由于美军第四团团长查尔斯·F·B·普赖斯（Charles F. B. Price）上校提出强烈交涉——日军已渗透进该团防区——日军迅速撤至虞洽卿路以西。与此同时，租界警务处总监杰拉德（F. W. Gerrard）少校开始就占领老闸地区一事与日方进行谈判，该区域最终得以清空，使得南京路交通得以恢复，自炸弹爆炸以来被困在南京路各百货公司内的华人得以返回。由日军巡逻队陪同的武装锡克教巡捕也在各个街区设立哨卡，试图阻止行人进入该区域。然而，此举并未成功，人群很快重返街头。

投弹者现身

炸弹袭击事件发生得极为突然。在中方军事路线两侧的南京路上，中国人群被严密阻挡在外。突然，在南京路以南的广西路上，一名身穿“中山装”的男子从围观人群中走出，朝南京路方向走了几步。当一名华捕试图将其推回人群时，他拿出一个用中文报纸包裹的物品，扔向行进的士兵队列。该物品落在对面的人行道附近并发生爆炸。这是一枚制作粗糙的米尔斯型（Mills type）手榴弹，炸伤了三名日本士兵、一名日本平民、一名锡克教巡捕、一名华捕，以及当时正在街角执勤的老闸捕房侦探副督察麦克菲（J. McPhee）先生。麦克菲先生的大衣被炸弹碎片撕裂，其中一块碎片被他内袋里携带的一张巴士通行证挡住。他手臂受了一处皮肉伤。

甚至在炸弹爆炸之前，一名华捕显然依照指令，迅速拔出手枪射击袭击者——这种训练有素的警觉性令人印象深刻。共开了四枪，枪枪命中。

日军队伍中引起了一阵恐慌，日本旁观者的“万岁”欢呼声戛然而止。指挥官大声喝令，该区域迅速被包围。所有侧街都部署了哨兵，同时各组士兵开始搜查弄堂和建筑物。约下午1时，一名日本士兵向新新大楼的一扇窗户开了一枪，但击中了墙壁。这一枪加剧了混乱，使许多平民惊慌逃窜寻求掩护。十分钟后，游行恢复。

值得注意的是，在事件发生前后，行进队列中的士兵在经过楼宇之间时，都会抬头仰望建筑物，似乎预料会有麻烦发生。

游行开始

上午11时前不久，在英国防卫区内侧、静安寺路铁路道口处等待游行的日本人和外侨人群中，可以听到吹响行进曲调的号角声。随后，游行队伍的前锋部队进入视野，并在铁路道口另一侧停下。与此同时，一名身穿卡其色制服、肤色较深的朝鲜人挥舞着日本国旗四处走动，热情地与提前沿街道下行、走在主力部队前方的一小群日本官员握手。来自各处的“夕阳”波（“Sunset” Wave，音译）警卫队士兵护卫着这群日本官员。

page_data.en:
"Insult to Flag"
A Briton's alleged insult to the Japanese flag was responsible for a minor incident at the corner of Nanking and Szechuen Roads, but by a swift manœuvre foreign police officers managed to isolate those concerned from the rest of the crowd and after a great deal of argument the excited Japanese reservists were persuaded into letting the police handle the matter in their own way.
The incident occurred at about 1.30 p.m., just after one company of soldiers had passed and another was approaching the crossing. According to eye-witnesses of the incident, Mr. E. T. Maitland, formerly Municipal Advocate, grew annoyed at the way in which a Japanese flag was waved about in his face and eventually snatched it away, smashing the frail stock on which the flag was mounted. Angered in turn, the civilian hit Mr. Maitland, whereupon another foreigner standing next to him struck a return blow, and a scrimmage ensued right in the entrance of Hall & Holtz's Men's Shop.
Foreign police officers rushed to the scene from all directions and succeeded in getting the two foreigners away from the growing mob and pushing them into a bookstore next door. They then formed a wall in front of the shop and refused to let anyone through.
The small crowd of reservists and civilians, some what daunted by this display of force, hesitated, argued and did a little pushing, but the police were adamant. This did not satisfy one old gentleman, clad in an old raincoat, grey flannel trousers and a blue, woollen waistcoat. Striding impatiently back to the corner, he started to harangue the crowd.
By the time some of them started moving again in the direction of the shop, one of the foreigners had left. Several Japanese policemen, who had been hastily summoned, arrived on the scene and succeeded in persuading the reservists to go back and watch the marching soldiers and to leave the police to settle the matter.

Incidents on Bund
The Bund, opposite the Cathay Hotel, was the scene of some incidents in which armed Japanese and foreigners were involved.
The first incident occurred when a Japanese in civilian clothes stepped on to the running board of a motor car on the Bund just as Japanese soldiers turned from Nanking Road toward the Bund. The foreign occupant objected to this and asked the Japanese to alight, whereupon the latter produced a pistol menacingly. The situation lasted but briefly, as the Japanese turned away, saying something in his own language.
Shortly afterward, a second incident occurred when a foreign photographer, attempting to dash across The Bund in a wide gap of the parade and was chased by a Japanese soldier with a levelled rifle. Before the foreigner could reach Jinkie Road, he was pulled back by the soldier and was compelled to return to his original place.
Since early morning Japanese civilians of both sexes and semi-uniformed "ronins" had dispersed into the Bund part of the Settlement, all carrying Rising-Sun flags. They took up positions along the route of the procession and whenever they felt like it, especially when a parade or other high-ranking officer passed, the shouts became particularly loud and deafening. At other times, although they remained Japanese, they would shout when an extra strong emotion was aroused.

The Japanese banks and commercial houses downtown were all gaily decorated and their doors were thrown open for the first time since the beginning of the hostilities. The Yokohama Specie Bank on The Bund was particularly brightly dressed and from in front of the building a large number of Japanese citizens greeted the parade. This group included many young women in brilliantly coloured kimonos, and small boys and girls in their "Sunday best." All carried Japanese flags and waved them constantly during the march past. One Japanese had a microphone which he held close to those cheering and through which the "banzais" were sent to Tokyo and other cities in Japan.
One foreign shop in Nanking Road, between Szechuen and Kiangse Roads, displayed the Italian flag in its doorway, but otherwise the colours seen downtown were all red and white.

Police Busy
The police arrangements along the entire route were splendidly carried out. At the corner of Avenue Edward VII and Boulevard de Montigny, Maj. Fabre, M. Jobez, M. Leblanc and other officials of the French Police watched the parade file past. In the Settlement, Mr. H. D. M. Robertson, Assistant Commissioner, and Supt. A. H. Alers, of "A" Division, were in charge of the police precautions along Yu Ya Ching and Nanking Roads and The Bund, while Mr. R. W. Yorke, Assistant Commissioner, handled the difficult traffic problem.
Major F. W. Gerrard, Commissioner, and Maj. K. M. Bourne, Deputy Commissioner, personally watched the situation in the Settlement throughout the day and directed the police operations.

Foreigners Assaulted
Shortly before 3.30 o'clock in the afternoon, Mr. Vaughn Reid, American was assaulted by two Japanese officers, wearing white gloves, and by a Japanese soldier who hit him with the butt of a rifle. The incident occurred at the corner of Yu Ya Ching and Nanking Roads, where the Japanese were clearing the streets.
Mr. Reid, who was wearing spectacles, was hit about the face by the two Japanese officers and a Japanese soldier followed this up by striking him with the butt of his rifle. An unidentified Austrian gentleman managed to pacify them, and escorted Mr. Reid from the scene with the assistance of a foreign police officer from Louisa Station.
Several foreign cameramen who were attempting to get photographs of the Japanese soldiers were also molested by the soldiers, but none were seriously injured.
There was a minor "incident" on The Bund, at the foot of Peking Road, shortly before 4 o'clock, when the last sections of the procession were passing. A young foreigner tried to cross the column of marching men but was stopped by a Japanese officer of the I.J.N. and sent back to the pavement. He was roughly handled before a tall man from the Foreign Office Unit got to his side and by his presence alone halted the mauling. A foreign police officer came up immediately afterward and settled the difficulty, telling the foreigner he must wait till the parade had passed.

"Throwing Eggs" Seized
A different note was struck when a Chinese policeman seized a bucketful of "throwing eggs" from a Chinese near Yu Yuen Road yesterday morning as the parade was about to start. It was assumed that the eggs had been brought to that particular point for no good purpose. Not one of them, however left the bucket in which they were being carried.

On The Bund
As offices released their employees at noon, the crowds on The Bund north of Nanking Road grew thicker and thicker, while more and more Japanese, all "armed" with the Japanese flag, came over the bridge from Hongkew to line the pavements eight or nine deep and await the arrival of the Japanese forces.
By 12.15 p.m. all traffic attempting to turn into Nanking Road from the Bund was diverted into side-streets even the buses being made to park along the water-front. The only cars permitted to drive up Nanking Road were the innumerable new sedans, old tourers, big cars and small ones, each and every one of which carried a full load of Japanese civilians and reservists, not to mention flags sticking out of all windows at all angles.
Large squads of foreign, Sikh and Chinese policemen were kept busy along the road, and no one was permitted on the north pavement of Nanking Road except a few foreign officers and press cameramen. The two main cheering points of the be-flagged Japanese civilians were in front of the Yokohama Specie Bank building and around the Nanking Road and the Bund traffic signal tower.
page_data.zh:
“侮辱国旗”
一名英国人涉嫌侮辱日本国旗，导致在南京路与四川路路口发生了一起小事件。但外国巡捕迅速采取行动，将涉事者与其余人群隔离开来。经过一番激烈的争辩，情绪激动的日本后备役军人最终被说服，同意由警方自行处理此事。
该事件发生在下午1时30分左右，正值一队士兵刚刚通过，另一队正接近该路口。据目击者称，前工部局法律顾问E. T. Maitland先生对有人在他面前挥舞日本国旗的方式感到恼火，最终夺过旗帜，折断了固定旗帜的脆弱旗杆。那名平民随即愤怒地击打了Maitland先生，站在他旁边的另一名外国人则予以回击，随后在Hall & Holtz男装店门口爆发了一场混战。
外国巡捕从四面八方赶赴现场，成功将两名外国人从越聚越多的人群中带离，并推进隔壁的一家书店。随后，他们在店门前组成人墙，拒绝让任何人通过。
由后备役军人和平民组成的小股人群因这种武力展示而略显胆怯，他们犹豫、争论并进行了一些推搡，但警方态度坚决。这并未让一位身穿旧雨衣、灰色法兰绒长裤和蓝色羊毛背心的老先生满意。他不耐烦地大步回到路口，开始向人群发表煽动性演讲。
当其中一些人再次朝书店方向移动时，一名外国人已经离开。几名被紧急召来的日本警察到达现场，成功说服后备役军人回去观看行进的士兵，并将此事留给警方解决。

外滩事件
在外滩，凯泰酒店（Cathay Hotel）对面，发生了一些涉及武装日本人和外国人的事件。
第一起事件发生在一名便衣日本人踏上一辆停在外滩的汽车踏板时，当时日本士兵正从南京路转向外滩。车内的外国人对此表示反对，要求该日本人下车，后者随即威胁性地掏出手枪。局势持续的时间很短，因为该日本人转身离开，用本国语言说了些什么。
不久后，发生了第二起事件，一名外国摄影师试图穿过游行队伍中的一个宽阔空隙冲过外滩，被一名端着步枪的日本士兵追赶。在该外国人到达江西路之前，他被士兵拉回，并被迫回到原来的位置。
自清晨以来，男女日本平民以及半制服的“浪人”已分散进入租界的外滩部分，所有人都携带着旭日旗。他们沿游行路线占据位置，每当他们兴致所至，特别是当游行队伍或其他高级军官经过时，呼喊声变得格外响亮和震耳欲聋。在其他时候，虽然他们保持沉默，但当情绪特别激动时也会呼喊。

市中心的日本银行和商号都装饰得喜气洋洋，自敌对行动开始以来，它们的大门首次敞开。位于外滩的横滨正金银行装饰得尤为鲜艳，大量日本市民在大楼前迎接游行队伍。这群人中包括许多身着色彩鲜艳和服的年轻女性，以及穿着“周日盛装”的小男孩和小女孩。所有人都手持日本国旗，并在游行经过时不断挥舞。一名日本人拿着麦克风，将其靠近欢呼者，通过它将“万岁”声传送到东京和日本其他城市。
南京路上，位于四川路与江西路之间的一家外国商店在门口悬挂了意大利国旗，但除此之外，市中心看到的颜色全是红白两色。

警方忙碌
整个路线的警务安排执行得非常出色。在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）与孟神父路（Boulevard de Montigny）的路口，法租界警务处的Fabre少校、Jobez先生、Leblanc先生及其他官员观看了游行队伍列队经过。在公共租界内，副总监H. D. M. Robertson先生和“A”区警司A. H. Alers先生负责虞洽卿路和南京路及外滩沿线的警务预防措施，而副总监R. W. Yorke先生则处理棘手的交通问题。
警务处处长F. W. Gerrard少校和副处长K. M. Bourne少校全天亲自监视租界内的局势并指挥警务行动。

外国人遭袭击
下午3时30分前不久，美国人Vaughn Reid先生遭到两名戴白手套的日本军官和一名用步枪枪托击打他的日本士兵的袭击。事件发生在虞洽卿路与南京路的路口，当时日本人正在清理街道。
戴眼镜的Reid先生面部遭到两名日本军官的击打，随后一名日本士兵用步枪枪托对他进行了殴打。一位身份不明的奥地利绅士设法平息了事态，并在来自露易丝巡捕房（Louisa Station）的一名外国巡捕的协助下，护送Reid先生离开现场。
几名试图拍摄日本士兵照片的外国摄影师也受到了士兵的骚扰，但无人受重伤。
下午4时前不久，当游行队伍的最后几部分经过时，外滩北京路底发生了一起轻微的“事件”。一名年轻外国人试图穿过行进的人群队伍，但被一名日本海军（I.J.N.）军官拦住并被赶回人行道。在一位来自外侨事务组（Foreign Office Unit）的高个子男子赶到他身边之前，他遭到了粗暴对待，仅凭该男子的在场就制止了殴打。随后一名外国巡捕立即赶到并解决了纠纷，告知该外国人必须等待游行队伍通过。

查获“投掷用鸡蛋”
昨天上午，当游行即将开始时，一名中国巡捕在豫园路附近从一名中国人手中查获了一桶“投掷用鸡蛋”，气氛为之一变。人们推测这些鸡蛋被带到该特定地点是出于不良目的。然而，桶里的鸡蛋一个也没有被扔出。

在外滩
随着中午各机构释放员工，南京路以北外滩的人群越来越密集，而越来越多的日本人——全都“武装”着日本国旗——从虹口过桥而来，在人行道上排成八九层深，等待日本军队的到来。
到下午12时15分，所有试图从外滩转入南京路的交通都被分流到侧街，甚至公共汽车也被迫沿水边停放。唯一允许驶上南京路的车辆是无数辆新的轿车、旧式敞篷车、大型车和小型车，每一辆都载满了日本平民和后备役军人，更不用说从各个角度伸出车窗的旗帜了。
大批外国、锡克教和中国巡捕在沿线忙碌，除少数外国军官和新闻摄影师外，任何人不得进入南京路北侧人行道。持旗日本平民的两个主要欢呼点位于横滨正金银行大楼前以及南京路与外滩交通信号塔周围。

page_data.en:
Marines Action
Upheld By Hull

Washington Concerned
Over Nanking Road
Parade Incident

(United Press)
WASHINGTON, Dec. 3.—Grave
concern was manifest by the De-
partment of State today over the
narrow margin with which a
serious incident was averted be-
tween Japanese troops and the
United States Marines in Shang-
hai yesterday.

The Japanese, in expanding
their cordon around the scene of
the bomb throwing on Nanking
Road, moved directly into the
American defense sector west of
Yu Ya Ch'ng Road and refused to
budge until their withdrawal was
demanded by Colonel Charles F.
B. Price, Commanding Officer of
the Fourth Marines, and Captain
Ronald A. Boone, Public Relations
Officer, had appeared and de-
manded their removal from the
American zone.

The Japanese also halted and
turned back Marine dispatch car-
riers and U. S. Marine official
trucks, although one Marine
motorcycle rider, bearing official
dispatches to the U. S. Consulate-
General, refused to stop and ran
the gauntlet.

Mr. Cordell Hull, Secretary of
State, announced that American
officials in both Shanghai and
Tokyo had warned the Japanese
authorities that a military de-
monstration through the streets of
the International Settlement was
highly inadvisable.

Comment was reserved pending
receipt of official dispatches; but
it was evident that the action of
the U. S. Marines in Shanghai in
expelling the Japanese from the
American defense sector was fully
approved by Washington.
page_data.zh:
陆战队行动
获赫尔支持

华盛顿关注
南京路
游行事件

（合众社）
华盛顿，12月3日。——国务院今日表现出严重关切，因为昨天在上海，日本军队与美国海军陆战队之间险些发生严重事件，幸得避免。

日本人在扩大其在南京路投弹现场周围的警戒线时，直接进入了虞洽卿路以西的美军防区，并拒绝撤离，直到美国海军陆战队第四团团长Charles F. B. Price上校和公共关系官Ronald A. Boone上尉出现并要求其撤出美国区域。

日本人还拦截并遣返了海军陆战队的信使和美国海军陆战队的官方卡车，尽管一名携带送往美国总领事馆官方公文的陆战队摩托车骑手拒绝停车，强行冲过了封锁线。

国务卿Cordell Hull先生宣布，驻上海和东京的美国官员已警告日本当局，在国际租界街道上进行军事示威是极不明智的。

在收到官方电报之前暂不发表评论；但显然，华盛顿完全批准上海美国海军陆战队将日本人驱逐出美国防区的行动。

page_data.en:
Japanese Report
Four Casualties

J.P.C. One Of Bombing
Victims; Assassin
Said Chinese

Dealing with yesterday's incident at the corners of Nanking and Kwangsi Roads at 12.44 p.m. A Japanese press spokesman this morning corrected previous statements in asserting that the Japanese suffered four men wounded in all. One of these died a few minutes afterwards while the three others were still alive. Of the latter one may be in serious condition as several grenade splinters lodged in his left side. All were injured about the legs but not seriously.
Answering questions, the spokesman stated that contrary to previous reports, the man is now definitely known to be Chinese who threw the home-made bomb, received medical attention on the spot. A Chinese physician summoned by the S.M.P., he said, and a Japanese doctor arrived soon after and gave him first aid, but they could not save him. He was taken to the Municipal Hospital where he died. The police are now searching for the assassin.
page_data.zh:
日方报告
四人伤亡

日侨俱乐部成员为爆炸受害者之一；刺客据称为中国人

针对昨天中午12时44分发生在南京路与广西路路口的事件，一名日本新闻发言人今晨更正了先前的说法，声称日本人共有四人受伤。其中一人在几分钟后死亡，另外三人仍然存活。在后三者中，有一人情况可能严重，因为数块手榴弹碎片嵌入其左侧身体。所有人的腿部均受伤，但并不严重。
在回答提问时，该发言人表示，与之前的报道相反，现已明确知道投掷自制炸弹的人是中国人，他在现场接受了医疗救治。他说，工部局警务处（S.M.P.）召唤了一名中国医生，随后一名日本医生也赶到并给予了急救，但未能挽救其生命。他被送往市立医院，在那里死亡。警方目前正在搜捕刺客。

Translation of extracts from the local German newspaper
"□□□□□□□□□□□□", dated December 4, 1937.
------------------

GERMAN OFFICER RESCUES AMERICAN

Last night, when the streets were being cleared of
by-standers at the time the zone in the centre of the city
was being extended, the Japanese acted with considerable
roughness and the excitement which existed among the
foreigners who were being driven back by threats and blows
administered by the Japanese soldiers and officers was
exceedingly great.

An elderly American became so excited in consequence
of the attacks made by the advancing Japanese on a large
number of foreigners that he resisted. This led to his
being surrounded by several Japanese officers who grabbed
and pummelled him with their fists. The American stood
his ground and hit one of the Japanese officers causing his
lips to bleed. The American thereupon was grasped by the
Japanese and pushed against the wall at Ju La Ching Road
(Race Course).

There was no doubt that the American stood in utter
danger of losing his life as one of the Japanese had already
called out "Shoot him!" and both officers and men pulled
out their revolvers. At this moment, a German, named
Woo. Schmidt, threw himself between the officers and the
American. He grabbed one of the Japanese by the collar and
pulled him away thus saving the life of the American.
The American, we hear, is the manager of the Lido.

It is also reported that the Japanese treated a
German named Herr Hannach rather harshly.
----------

In an article from the pen of Herr Haldermann about
Nanking, he makes the following remark in the closing sentence:
"The impression is held in Shanghai and abroad that the Chinese
fighting material is demoralized. This is not so, it is quite
the contrary."

1937年12月4日当地德文报纸“□□□□□□□□□□□□”摘录译文。
------------------

德国军官救助美国人

昨晚，在市中心区域扩展、街道正在清理旁观者之时，日本人的行动相当粗暴。在日本士兵和军官的威胁与殴打下被迫后退的外国人中，激愤情绪极其高涨。

一位年长的美国人因目睹前进中的日本人攻击大量外国人而变得异常激动，并进行了抵抗。这导致他被几名日本军官包围，他们抓住他并用拳头殴打。该美国人坚守原地，并击中了一名日本军官，致其嘴唇流血。随后，该美国人被日本人抓住，并被推搡至跑马厅路（Ju La Ching Road）的墙边。

毫无疑问，这位美国人面临着生命危险，因为其中一名日本人已经喊出“开枪打死他！”，且军官和士兵都拔出了左轮手枪。就在此时，一名名叫伍·施密特（Woo. Schmidt）的德国人冲到了军官和美国人之间。他抓住一名日本人的衣领并将其拉开，从而救了这位美国人的性命。据悉，该美国人是丽都（Lido）的经理。

另有报道称，日本人对待一位名为汉纳赫先生（Herr Hannach）的德国人也相当粗暴。
----------

在一篇由哈尔德曼先生（Herr Haldermann）撰写的关于南京的文章中，他在结尾句中写道：“上海及海外有一种印象，认为中国的战斗物资士气低落。事实并非如此，恰恰相反。”

page_data.en:
Wounded Police
Officer's Story
Of the Incident

Sub-Inspector J. McPhee
Has Narrow Escape

AN UGLY SITUATION

Machine Guns Mounted in
Nanking Road

An eye-witness account of the incident in Nanking Road yesterday, when a man of unknown origin standing in Kwangse Road hurled a hand grenade at the parade of Japanese troops which was making its way in the direction of The Bund, was given to a "North-China Daily News" reporter by the man who was closest to where the grenade exploded, Sub-Inspector John McPhee, who was injured by the missile bursting a few feet away. Mr. McPhee was instrumental in saving the life of a Japanese photographer who was just in front of him when the grenade landed in the roadway.

"The last few ranks of one of the infantry columns were passing Kwangse Road," he stated, "when I saw the grenade whizzing through the air over the heads of the troops who were passing in front of me. The next thing I knew, it had landed practically at my feet. I instinctively drew back, and dragged with me the Japanese photographer. As the grenade exploded, I felt a stabbing pain in my right arm. I found that pieces had gone through the right sleeve of my coat, and other fragments had penetrated the right side of my coat. The fragment that penetrated my sleeve lodged underneath the skin. It was an extremely close shave!"

A "North-China Daily News" reporter who was watching the parade from a tram stop near Yu Ya-ching Road near the explosion of the grenade a short distance up Nanking Road, and saw the puff of white smoke which seemed to arise from the midst of the column of Japanese troops. For a moment, there was utter confusion, soldiers running hither and thither in an uncertain manner. Then sharp words of command rang out, and the troops moved on to the pavement on the left hand side of the road. Meanwhile, machine gun units took up their position in the street opposite the Sun Ya Restaurant, at the corner of

Yunan and Nanking Roads, and at other points close to where the incident occurred, with their guns trained in the direction of The Bund.

An Ugly Situation

It was an ugly situation, fraught with all kinds of unpleasant possibilities. By the roadside, scores of Japanese troops; at strategic points machine gun units apparently awaiting the order to open fire; around the machine gunners, a throng of Japanese civilians cheering and waving flags, and one or two foreigners who were pushed and jostled backwards and forwards in the fever heat of excitement which electrified the crowd. A cordon of Japanese troops and police prevented anyone from approaching the scene. Police officers buzzed around close to Kwangse Road, from which the grenade was thrown.

Suddenly, a shot rang out. This further excited the crowd, who suspected that another incident had taken place. In was afterwards discovered, however, that the shot was fired by a Japanese soldier into a building on the left hand side of the road, evidently at some suspicious character standing at an upper floor window.

Slowly, the troops who had fallen out on to the pavement got back into line once again ready to move on. Several anti-aircraft gun crews, mounted in motor lorries, were brought up and trained in the direction of Kwangse Road. A cavalryman patrolled up and down on the pavement in front of the Sun Ya Restaurant. The column began to move along, and in a few minutes the last remaining troops in the line, followed by busses filled with Japanese civilians, had disappeared from sight.

A Motionless Figure

Meanwhile, the motionless figure of the man who hurled the grenade had been placed beneath a covering on the pavement a few yards from the corner of Nanking and Kwangsi Roads, having been shot by a Chinese constable. He was not dead—but died later. Settlement police officials conferred with high Japanese military officers who had arrived to take charge of the investigation into the circumstances of the incident. Marching at the double, a platoon of Japanese soldiers, with bayonets fixed, arrived and took up their position in Kwangsi Road.

The official party moved over to the small hole in the roadway which marked the spot where the grenade had exploded. Four or so Japanese soldiers with fixed bayonets kept the crowd back. Later, they formed a cordon across the road, and pushed the score or so of foreigners who were watching the investigation back to within 20 yards or so of Yu Yaching Road.

The first foreigner to be stopped by the cordon was a police sergeant on a motor-cycle. After waiting for a few minutes, he was allowed to go through. Not long afterwards, a platoon of British troops hove in sight marching eastwards down Nanking Road. They halted at the cordon, but after the officer in charge had given explanations, the Japanese troops stepped aside to let them pass. Next to arrive on the scene was an American Marine dispatch rider, who passed through the cordon without stopping, and failed to see the signal of the military policeman beyond, who held up his hand for the motor cyclist to halt.

British Lorries Turned Back

Orders were given later than no persons whatever were to be allowed through the cordon, and several British military lorries were turned back by the Japanese troops on guard. Three or four Japanese officers then appeared on the scene, and the order was given for the crowd to be pushed back further. This led to strong objections on the part of a handful of foreigners who were flung back violently by one of the officers.

The situation became serious when one of the foreigners, Mr. D. W. Murphy, resisted the attempts of the officer to push him back. The officer became more violent, and was joined by several others, who manhandled Mr. Murphy, and forced him back along Yu Ya-ching Road. He still strongly objected to this treatment, and was surrounded by a group of Japanese troops, who dragged and pushed him along the road. The whole incident was witnessed by a "North-China Daily News" reporter standing at the corner of Nanking and Yu Ya-ching Roads.

As the tension increased, two of the Japanese officers whipped out their pistols, and kept them in their hands. Curious crowds thronged Yu Ya-ching and Nanking Roads watching the scene.
page_data.zh:
受伤警官讲述
事件经过

副督察 J. McPhee
死里逃生

局势严峻

机枪部署于
南京路

《字林西报》记者采访了约翰·麦克菲（John McPhee）副督察，他是手榴弹爆炸地点附近最近的人，并在几英尺外被爆炸碎片炸伤。他就昨日南京路发生的事件提供了目击者证词：当时一名身份不明男子站在广西路，向正朝外滩方向行进的一队日本军队投掷了一枚手榴弹。麦克菲先生在救下一名就在手榴弹落地时位于他前方的日本摄影师的生命方面发挥了作用。

“其中一个步兵纵队的最后几排正经过广西路，”他说道，“这时我看见手榴弹从我面前经过的部队头顶呼啸而过。接下来我知道的是，它几乎落在了我的脚边。我本能地向后缩，并将那名日本摄影师一起拖开。当手榴弹爆炸时，我感到右臂一阵刺痛。我发现碎片击穿了我外套的右袖，其他碎片则穿透了外套的右侧。穿透我袖子的碎片嵌在了皮肤下面。真是千钧一发！”

一名《字林西报》记者在距离爆炸点不远、南京路上靠近亚尔培路（Yu Ya-ching Road）的电车站观看游行，看到一团白烟似乎从日本军队纵队中间升起。片刻间，现场一片混乱，士兵们不确定地四处奔跑。随后响起了尖锐的命令声，部队移动到了道路左侧的人行道上。与此同时，机枪部队在孙雅饭店（Sun Ya Restaurant）对面的街道上占据阵地，该处位于

云南路与南京路的拐角处，以及其他靠近事件发生地的地点，枪口指向外滩方向。

局势严峻

局势十分严峻，充满了各种令人不快的可能性。路边有数十名日本士兵；战略要点部署了机枪部队，显然在等待开火命令；机枪手周围是一群欢呼挥旗的日本平民，还有一两名外国人在令人群激动的狂热气氛中被推来推去。一道由日本士兵和警察组成的警戒线阻止任何人接近现场。警察官员在投掷手榴弹的广西路附近忙碌穿梭。

突然，一声枪响。这进一步激怒了人群，他们怀疑又发生了另一起事件。然而后来发现，这一枪是一名日本士兵向道路左侧的一栋建筑物射击的，显然是针对站在楼上窗户处的某个可疑人物。

慢慢地，撤到人行道上的部队重新整队，准备继续前进。几组安装在卡车上的高射炮 crew 被调来，炮口指向广西路方向。一名骑兵在孙雅饭店前的人行道上来回巡逻。纵队开始行进，几分钟后，队列中剩余的部队以及满载日本平民的公共汽车消失在视线中。

一个静止的身影

与此同时，投掷手榴弹的那名男子的静止身影已被放置在南京路与广西路拐角处几码外的人行道上，身上盖着遮盖物，他此前被一名中国巡捕开枪击中。他当时并未死亡——但后来身亡。租界警务处官员与抵达现场负责调查事件情况的高级日本军官进行了磋商。一队日本士兵跑步到达，刺刀上膛，在广西路占据阵地。

官方人员移动到路面上标记手榴弹爆炸位置的小坑处。四五名刺刀上膛的日本士兵将人群挡在后面。随后，他们在道路上形成了一道警戒线，将大约二十名围观调查的外国人推回到距离亚尔培路（Yu Yaching Road）约20码的地方。

第一个被警戒线拦下的外国人是一名骑摩托车的警长。等待了几分钟后，他被允许通过。不久之后，一队英国军队出现在视野中，沿南京路向东行进。他们在警戒线前停下，但在负责军官做出解释后，日本士兵退到一旁让他们通过。接着到达现场的是一名美国海军陆战队摩托车通讯员，他未作停留便穿过了警戒线，没有看到后方宪兵举手示意摩托车手停下的信号。

英国卡车被折返

随后下达命令，严禁任何人通过警戒线，几辆英国军用卡车被值守的日本士兵勒令折返。接着有三四名日本军官出现在现场，并下令将人群进一步向后推挤。这引起少数外国人的强烈抗议，其中一人被一名军官猛烈推开。

当一名外国人 D. W. Murphy 先生抵抗军官试图将他推开的举动时，局势变得严重起来。该军官变得更加暴力，其他几名军官也加入进来，对 Murphy 先生动手动脚，并强迫他沿亚尔培路（Yu Ya-ching Road）后退。他仍然强烈反对这种待遇，并被一群日本士兵包围，他们在路上拖拽并推搡他。整个事件被一名站在南京路与亚尔培路拐角处的《字林西报》记者目睹。

随着紧张局势加剧，两名日本军官拔出手枪，并握在手中。好奇的人群聚集在亚尔培路和南京路观看这一幕。

page_data.en:
Japanese View
Of Nanking Rd.
Bomb Incident

Spokesman's Reassurance at
Press Conference

NO UNDUE ADVANTAGE
WILL BE TAKEN

The following statement was
issued by the Japanese military
authorities at the press conference at
5 p.m. yesterday:—

At 12.44 p.m. a Chinese in plain clothes
threw a hand-grenade at Japanese forces
marching from the Western District
into Hongkew at the intersection of
Kwangse and Nanking Roads. The
grenade exploded, wounding two
Japanese soldiers and one foreign
detective-inspector of the S.M.P. The
assailant was shot and killed by a Chi-
nese police constable who previously
had tried to push this man out from
the police cordon on Kwangse Road.
Following the attack, the area was
roped off by Japanese forces which,
in conjunction with the Shanghai
Municipal Police, are conducting an
investigation into the attack.

The area, said the spokesman, ex-
tended from Yu Ya-ching Road to
Fukien Road, and from Kiukiang
Road to Peking Road.

"I should add," went on the spokes-
man," that the Japanese authorities
have no intention of taking undue
advantage of the incident."

"In view of the fact that the as-
sailant was killed on the spot, what
was the necessity of roping off all
that part of the Settlement?" a cor-
respondent asked. "It is necessary
to conduct an investigation in the
area because it may harbour accom-
plices or give clues as to where this
man came from and what his
affiliations were," was the reply.

The man had definitely been identi-
fied as a Korean from evidence
found on the spot, but the spokes-
man said that at the present stage
of the evidence he was not able to
reveal "what has been found." A
large fragment of the hand-grenade
had been found, together with the
pin; it appeared to be of the potato-
masher type.

Were there any shots from Sun
Sun at the Japanese troops?—The
matter is now under investigation.

Attack on Army

In view of the usual prerogative
of the police in such matters, why
have the Japanese taken the action
they have taken?—The objective of
the attack was the Japanese army;
the case is different from an attack
on a civilian.

Is the area being extended
gradually?—It is hoped that will not
be necessary.

The Japanese are placing barbed
wire in the area; are they planning
a lengthy occupation?—The necessary
investigation is proceeding in colla-
boration with the S.M.P. and we
have no intention of taking undue
advantage.

How slightly were the two Japan-
ese wounded?—Not slightly. They
are painful wounds in the legs and
thighs, but will not prove fatal
unless complications set in.

Is it true S.M.C. protested yes-
terday against the transfer of the
troops?—No.

Were the Japanese residents told
it was just a transfer of troops or
a triumphal march?—It was explained
to them it was a movement of
troops.

Any protest to the S.M.C. over the
incident?—No steps have yet been
taken.

Will you hold the S.M.C. or
S.M.P. responsible for the incident?
—We do not believe the S.M.C. will
shirk from its responsibility in this
connection. We cannot hold the
S.M.C. responsible until the full in-
vestigation has been completed and
the facts established.

Could you elaborate on "undue
advantage"?—At the present stage,
we do not feel at liberty to elaborate
on this.

Were you satisfied at the prompt-
ness of the action taken by the
S.M.P.?—We feel that the Chinese
police constable carried out his
actions according to his sense of duty.
page_data.zh:
日本方面对
南京路炸弹
事件的看法

发言人在记者会上
给予保证

不会利用此事
谋取不当利益

日本军方当局在昨日下午5时的记者会上发布了以下声明：—

中午12时44分，一名便衣中国人在广西路与南京路交叉路口，向从西区行进至虹口的日本部队投掷了一枚手榴弹。手榴弹爆炸，炸伤了两名日本士兵和一名工部局警务处（S.M.P.）的外籍探长。袭击者被一名中国巡捕开枪击毙，该巡捕此前曾试图将该男子从广西路的警察警戒线中推出去。袭击发生后，该区域被日本部队封锁，日本部队正与上海公共租界工部局警务处合作，对袭击事件进行调查。

发言人称，该区域范围从亚尔培路延伸至福建路，从九江路延伸至北京路。

“我还要补充一点，”发言人继续说道，“日本当局无意利用此事件谋取不当利益。”

“鉴于袭击者已被当场击毙，为何有必要封锁租界的那么大一片区域？”一名记者问道。“有必要在该区域进行调查，因为那里可能藏有同伙，或能提供关于此人来自何处及其隶属关系的线索，”这是答复。

根据在现场发现的证据，该男子已被确认为朝鲜人，但发言人表示，在目前的证据阶段，他无法透露“发现了什么”。现场发现了一大块手榴弹碎片以及引信销；它似乎是柄式（potato-masher type）手榴弹。

孙孙饭店（Sun Sun）是否有向日本部队开枪？—此事目前正在调查中。

袭击军队

鉴于警方在此类事务中通常拥有的特权，日本人为何采取他们所采取的行动？—袭击的目标是日本军队；此案不同于对平民的袭击。

该区域是否在逐步扩大？—希望没有必要这样做。

日本人正在该区域设置铁丝网；他们是否计划长期占领？—必要的调查正在与工部局警务处（S.M.P.）合作进行，我们无意谋取不当利益。

两名日本人的伤势有多轻？—并不轻。他们的腿部和 thigh 部位受伤疼痛，但除非出现并发症，否则不会致命。

工部局（S.M.C.）昨天是否抗议过部队调动？—没有。

日本居民被告知这只是部队调动还是凯旋游行？—向他们解释这是部队调动。

是否就此事向工部局提出抗议？—尚未采取任何步骤。

你们会让工部局或工部局警务处对此事负责吗？—我们相信工部局不会在此事上推卸责任。在全面调查完成并查明事实之前，我们不能让工部局承担责任。

能否详细阐述“不当利益”？—在目前阶段，我们认为不便对此进行详细阐述。

你对工部局警务处行动的迅速性感到满意吗？—我们认为那名中国巡捕是本着责任感执行其行动的。

page_data.en:
GOOD POLICE WORK
Those Who appreciate the circumstances in
which they were called upon to maintain order
yesterday in the Settlement where over one
million Chinese citizens reside. will pay an
unreserved tribute of gratitude and admiration
to the Police Force. Despite the heavy burden
which its officers and men have borne during
the last four months, the organization smoothly
functioned to deal with an event which took
place at short notice and which obviously
demanded the exercise of considerable restraint.
The precision of the arrangements was most
noticeable and the swiftness with which, when
the procession had passed, the normal traffic of
the city was resumed indicated elaborate care,
unquestioning discipline and skilled experience
in direction. Major F. W. Gerrard, the Com-
missioner. bore a great responsibility. His
officers and men gave him splendid support and
the result would have been creditable to any
police force in the world. This is emphasized
because, as was to be expected, in the peculiar
circumstances, an attempt was made to disturb
the peace. The instantaneity of the action
by which a Chinese constable of the
Municipal Police shot the unhappy man who
threw a handgrenade proved how alert and
thorough was the provision for the public
safety. That was the only casualty, except for
minor wounds sustained by three Japanese
soldiers and three members of the Police Force
and for more serious injury to a Japanese
onlooker. Of the desirability of the proces-
sion there were and are grave doubts. It is an
open secret that during the last few days various
foreign authorities—military and civil—have en-
deavoured to explain to the Japanese High Com-
mand the exact gravity of the strain which such
a parade would throw on the police force. To
pretend that in a city of this size any incident
could be certainly prevented would be to fly in
the face of the facts. As it was most people
experienced in such matters heaved a sigh of
relief when, with the exception of the tragedy
mentioned and one or two other minor affairs,
including the dramatic suicide of a Chinese who
threw himself down from a balcony at the corner
of Yu Ya Ching Road and Avenue Edward VII.
it was known that the city had maintained its
general composure. The Japanese military
authorities were apparently impelled to take
temporary action in Nanking Road—a superfluous
measure, it seemed, and likely to aggravate
rather than allay feeling, especially as the Police
—to whose arrangements it will be noted an
official Japanese tribute has been paid—were
for the time being prevented from functioning
in the area affected. This military intrusion
caused considerable inconvenience and roused
much resentment among all sections of the
community with whom it came in contact. It
certainly added to the anxieties of the day. The
tact of the Police, however, overcame the un-
expected difficulty and by the end of
the evening it was expected that the situation
would be restored. The Shanghai Municipal
Police and its Commissioner took the laurels on
a day which will be looked back upon with
equivocal feelings by the people of this city.
Unfortunately it does not appear to be possible
to explain certain elements of psychology to
the Japanese authorities. Exhortations in the
friendliest terms have been disregarded, other-
wise the parade would not have been held. It
is certain, however, that that persistence has not
produced quite the effect it must be taken to
have intended. The civic mind is apt to assess
such demonstrations by its own clear-sighted
notion of international amenities.
page_data.zh:
出色的警务工作

那些了解昨日在居住着逾百万中国市民的租界内维持秩序所处环境的人，会对警队致以毫无保留的感激与钦佩之情。尽管在过去四个月中，警队官兵承担了沉重的负担，但该组织仍运转顺畅，应对了这一突发且显然需要极大克制的事件。部署之精准尤为引人注目；游行队伍通过后，城市交通迅速恢复正常，这表明了周密的筹划、严明的纪律以及指挥方面的娴熟经验。警务处处长 F. W. Gerrard 少校肩负着重大责任。他的下属官兵给予了他极好的支持，其成果足以令世界上任何一支警队引以为荣。之所以强调这一点，是因为正如人们所预料的那样，在这种特殊情况下，有人试图扰乱治安。工部局警务处的一名华籍巡捕当即开枪击毙了那名投掷手榴弹的不幸男子，这一瞬间的行动证明了公共安全防备工作的警觉性和周密性。除三名日本士兵和三名警务人员受轻伤，以及一名日本旁观者受较重伤外，这是唯一的伤亡事件。对于举行此次游行是否适宜，当时及现在都存在严重的疑虑。众所周知，在过去几天里，各外国当局——包括军方和民政当局——一直努力向日本最高指挥部解释，此类游行将给警队带来多么巨大的压力。声称在这座规模的城市中肯定能防止任何事件发生，那是违背事实的。事实上，大多数熟悉此类事务的人在得知城市保持了总体平静后，都如释重负地松了一口气，除了前述的悲剧以及一两起其他轻微事件（包括一名中国人在亚尔培路和爱德华七世大道拐角处从阳台跳下自杀的惊人举动）。日本军方当局显然被迫在南京路采取临时行动——这似乎是一项多余的举措，而且可能加剧而非平息情绪，尤其是因为警方——值得注意的是，官方已对日本的安排表示敬意——暂时被阻止在受影响区域执行职务。这种军事介入造成了相当大的不便，并在与其接触的各阶层民众中激起了强烈的不满。这无疑增加了当日的焦虑。然而，警方的机智克服了这一意外困难，预计到傍晚时分局势将得以恢复。上海公共租界工部局警务处及其处长在这一天赢得了荣誉，而本市市民回顾这一天时将怀着复杂的心情。不幸的是，似乎无法向日本当局解释某些心理因素。以最友好的方式提出的劝告被置之不理，否则游行就不会举行。然而可以肯定的是，这种坚持并未产生其意图达到的效果。市民舆论倾向于以其对国际礼仪的清晰认识来评估此类示威活动。

page_data.en:
Today's March
Is Called Off
By Japanese

Police Work Well In
Parade Through
Settlement

There will be no Japanese military parade along the International Settlement and French Concession Bunds to the Nantao Bund today.
Although originally planned for this morning, the parade, it was stated at the Japanese press conference yesterday afternoon, has been cancelled owing to the Nanking Road affair yesterday.
Questioned by foreign correspondents yesterday as to whether or not the French authorities had refused to permit the planned parade. The spokesman stated that no such refusal had been received.
He declared that the Japanese had merely suggested that they might like to hold such a parade and that the French had replied that it was against the ordinances of the French Concession to permit parades of a military nature.

Parade Lasts Two Hours

The Japanese parade through the Settlement yesterday started on scheduled time from the Toyoda Mills and lasted for almost two hours. Approximately 5,000 men participated in the long march to the Garden Bridge and despite the brief delay on Nanking Road as a result of the hand-grenade tossed at the Japanese troops passing through the department store area, the parade was completed by 2 p.m.
The vanguard of the procession entered the British guarded area at Jessfield at exactly 11 a.m. The British soldiers on duty at this point presented arms and then went about their business.
The first Japanese unit to enter the Settlement was a truck loaded with signalmen. This was followed at some distance by a British mounted police sergeant and four mounted Sikhs, who had been assigned to traffic duty for the occasion. It was emphasised by the police that they did not constitute an escort.
The mounted police were followed by a Japanese infantry detachment. A small cavalry unit followed the infantry which was in turn followed by an artillery unit. The latter unit was comprised of about six fieldpieces which were drawn by horses. More infantry and more cavalry followed. It took the procession about 40 minutes to pass a given point.

Few Spectators

As the marchers entered the Settlement, very few spectators were on hand to watch them. The people who lined the streets around Jessfield were mostly newspapermen and photographers. A few Japanese were on hand and the number of "banzais" was small compared with the cheering that the troops received from large numbers of Japanese civilians who crowded the line of march along Avenue Foch, Yu Ya Ching and Nanking Roads.
Both the French Police and the Shanghai Municipal Police did an excellent job of clearing the streets of the crowds that had collected early in the morning with the idea of witnessing the event.

Fearing untoward events, Chinese as well as foreigners were turned back from the route of march along Avenue Foch, Yu Ya Ching Road and Nanking Road.

Traffic Congested

The crowds were pushed back along all side streets to the parallel streets one block on either side of the thoroughfares traversed by the parade. The police experienced little difficulty, the crowds being quite tractable and easily handled.
Heavy police patrols were stationed along the entire route of march and persons who sought to get out of hand were immediately shoved back. Of course, traffic on side streets was seriously congested.
The advance guard of the Japanese force reached the Garden Bridge at about 1.15 p.m. and all marchers were in Hongkew where they were greeted by more "bansais" by 2 p.m.
While the march was in progress, a Chinese standing on a third floor window of a building near the B.A.T. clock at the corner of Avenue Edward VII and Yu Ya Ching Road fell down. His body caught on a high tension wire, causing a short circuit and sparks. During the resulting commotion Japanese soldiers broke their ranks.
page_data.zh:
今日日军
取消游行

警方在
租界游行期间
表现良好

今天，日军不会沿公共租界和法租界外滩至南市外滩举行军事游行。
尽管原计划于今天上午举行，但在昨日下午的日本记者招待会上宣布，由于昨日南京路事件，游行已取消。
昨日，外国记者询问发言人，法国当局是否拒绝允许计划中的游行。发言人表示，未收到此类拒绝。
他宣称，日本人 merely 建议他们希望举行此类游行，而法方回复称，允许军事性质的游行违反法租界的章程。

游行持续两小时

昨日日军穿过租界的游行按预定时间从丰田纱厂出发，持续了近两个小时。约 5,000 人参加了前往外白渡桥的长途行进，尽管因向经过百货公司区域的日军投掷手榴弹而在南京路造成短暂延误，但游行于下午 2 时前完成。
游行队伍的先头部队于上午 11 时整进入静安寺的英军警戒区。在此执勤的英军士兵举枪致敬，随后继续执行日常任务。
第一支进入租界的日军部队是一辆载有信号兵的卡车。其后相隔一段距离跟随的是一名英国骑警警长和四名锡克骑警，他们被指派负责当天的交通勤务。警方强调，他们并不构成仪仗护卫。
骑警之后是一支日本步兵分队。一小股骑兵部队跟随步兵，其后又跟随一支炮兵部队。后者由大约六门马拉野战炮组成。更多的步兵和骑兵紧随其后。游行队伍通过某一指定地点耗时约 40 分钟。

观众寥寥

当行进队伍进入租界时，现场观看的观众极少。在静安寺周围街道列队的人群大多是新闻记者和摄影师。现场只有少数日本人，与在霞飞路、亚尔培路和南京路沿线拥挤的大量日本平民向部队发出的欢呼声相比，“万岁”喊声寥寥无几。
法国警察和上海公共租界工部局警务处在清晨驱散聚集围观的人群方面表现出色。

出于对意外事件的担忧，中国人和外国人均被拦回，不得进入沿霞飞路、亚尔培路和南京路的游行路线。

交通拥堵

人群被推回至所有侧街，直至与游行主干道平行、相隔一个街区的大街上。警方几乎没有遇到什么困难，人群相当顺从，易于管控。
整个游行路线沿线部署了大量警力巡逻，任何试图失控的人员立即被推回。当然，侧街的交通严重拥堵。
日军先头部队于下午 1 时 15 分左右抵达外白渡桥，至下午 2 时，所有行进人员均已到达虹口，并在那里受到更多“万岁”喊声的欢迎。
在游行进行期间，一名站在爱德华七世大道和亚尔培路拐角处英美烟草公司钟楼附近建筑物三楼窗户上的中国人坠落。他的身体挂在一根高压线上，导致短路并产生火花。在随之而来的混乱中，日本士兵脱离了队列。

page_data.en:
Japanese Troops Are
Withdrawn From
Nanking Road Area

Incident Considered Closed Following Conference
Between Japanese Officials And Settlement
Police Chief Held Under Street Lamps

HAND-GRENADE TOSSED AT PARADE
IN BUSY SECTOR INJURES 4 JAPANESE

Nanking Road was clear of Japanese gendarmerie and military
shortly after 9 p.m. yesterday.
At an impromptu conference held in front of the Sun Sun Depart-
ment store in the dim light of street lamps, representatives of the
Japanese army and the Shanghai Municipal Police at 7.30 p.m. agreed
upon the terms of settlement of the Nanking Road bombing affair.
Participating in the talks, it was learned, were Colonel Sanetaka
Kusumoto, chief of the Special Service Section of the Japanese army
here and a representative of General Iwane Matsui, Japanese com-
mander-in-chief, and Police Commissioner F. W. Gerrard. Consul
Foriake Yoshioka also was present.

With complete agreement reached
on the steps to be taken by the
S.M.C., Japanese troops and gend-
armerie were withdrawn from the
department store area.
The measures agreed upon will
be carried out solely by the Shang-
hai Municipal Police, it was stated
in Japanese circles last night.
The nocturnal meeting was held
in the street, a few yards from the
spot where at about 12.50 p.m. three
Japanese soldiers and a Japanese
consular policeman and one British
police sergeant were wounded when
a youth, said by the Japanese to
have been a Chinese, tossed a hand-
grenade.
With the agreement reached, and
with the conclusion of the investi-
gation carried out in the area by
the Japanese gendarmerie, Japanese
troops began their withdrawal from
the district at 8.30 p.m. and were
out shortly thereafter.

Representations By Col. Price
Representations made by Colonel
Charles F. B. Price, commanding
the 4th U. S. Marines, to the
Japanese officer commanding the
detachment of Japanese troops
engaged in investigating the Nan-
king Road grenading yesterday
afternoon resulted in a withdrawal
of the Nipponese forces from
Mohawk Road back to Yu Ya Ching
Road.
Colonel Price, accompanied by
members of his staff, appeared on
the scene at Mohawk Road shortly
before 5 p.m. and told the Japanese
officer in command that the
Nipponese troops were well inside
the defense sector of the United
States Marines. He suggested that
they leave the sector.
The Japanese officer stated he did
not realize that his men had ad-
vanced such a distance along Bub-
bling Well Road and the order was
accordingly given for a withdrawal.

Caused Inconvenience
The advance of the Japanese
party from the intersection of Yu
Ya Ching and Nanking Roads to
Mohawk Road had resulted in con-
siderable inconvenience to the re-
sidents of the Park Hotel and the
Foreign Y.M.C.A. It was impossible
for occupants of either building to
get either in or out for some time.
The street in front of these two
places was cleared by 5.15 p.m. and
about 10 minutes later it had been
cleared of Japanese as far east as
Yu Ya Ching Road.
The Shanghai Municipal Police
took over the business of patrolling
the street and pedestrians, except
those having business along the
thoroughfare, were not allowed to
move past Park Road on Bubbling
Well Road in a northerly direction.

Lone Soldier Emerges
Failing to withdraw when his
comrades moved back was one lone
Japanese soldier who had emerged
from an alley to find the street de-
serted of his officers. He asked a
policeman to direct him back to
Yu Ya Ching Road and the request
was complied with. When last
seen he was moving slowly along
the street to the north.
The Japanese investigation party
last night was in occupation of
Nanking Road from Fokien Road
to Yu Ya Ching Road. They also
held Yu Ya Ching Road from Kiu-
kiang Road to Peking Road and
were in occupation of Fokien Road
from Kiukiang to Peking Roads.
Japanese authorities, a spokesman
of the Japanese embassy told news-
papermen and foreign correspond-
ents last night, "do not intend to
take undue advantage of the in-
cident." Patrols will be kept in the
area for the duration of the in-
vestigation, the spokesman revealed.

4 Japanese Wounded
Four Japanese, including three
soldiers, and a British police ser-
geant, were wounded when the
grenade was tossed at a passing
column of Japanese troops at 12.50
a.m. The grenade was tossed by a
young man alleged by Japanese to
have been a Chinese from a posi-
tion near the Sun Sun Department
Store.

The young man, whose age was
put at about 25 years, managed to
get through the police lines at
Kwangse Road from where he
hurled the missile.
A Chinese police constable nearby
immediately fired on the man,
wounding him in four places. The
fellow died about one hour after-
wards.
Questioned at the press conference
last night regarding the action of
the Chinese police constable in
firing upon the man, a Japanese
spokesman declared that the con-
stable had carried out his duty.
The wounded Japanese were:
Private Bun Endo, serious in-
juries to the left hip.
Private Matsugero Itabashi, slight
wound on the left leg.
Private Morita Kawashima, slight
wound on the right leg.
Constable Keiji Yoshioka, of the
Japanese Consular Police, received
six wounds, including one on the
forehead.
The three soldiers belonged to the
Fukui detachment. The policeman
was assigned to escort the Japanese
troops through the Settlement.

Inspector Also Injured
Inspector John McPhee, of the
S.M.P., who was near the scene of
the incident, received slight injuries
on an arm and leg.
The condition of Constable Yoshioka
is quite serious and he is now in the
French Hospital where he is ex-
pected to remain for six or seven
weeks before resuming his duties.
The grenade exploded about one
meter from where the constable
was standing.
The exploding of the grenade
failed to stop the Japanese parade
although it did cause a brief com-
motion. The marching Japanese
troops along that particular section
of roadway were immediately halt-
ed and patrols were sent out search-
ing the streets of the neighbor-
hood.
Foreign newspapermen and other
foreigners on the scene immediately
scurried for cover. And the Japan-
ese patrols did some fast moving
themselves.

Resume March
The main body of the Japanese
force, however, resumed its march
shortly afterwards and crossed
Garden Bridge at 1.40 p.m.
Reinforced by troops brought from
the Hongkew District, Japanese offi-
cers and soldiers took over the in-
vestigation of the case and grad-
ually moved onlookers back along
both west and east areas of Nan-
king Road. By 4 p.m. they were
patrolling Yu Ya Ching, Hankow
and Fokien Roads. They were as-
sisted by Japanese gendarmes under
the command of Captains Okamura
and Makoto Tsukamoto.
An investigation was conducted
on the spot by officials of the Japan-
ese gendarmerie, the Shanghai
Municipal Police, and the Japanese
Consular Police.
page_data.zh:
日军撤出南京路区域

日方官员与租界警务处长在街灯下举行会议后，事件被视为已了结

手榴弹投掷于繁忙地段游行队伍中，致4名日本人受伤

昨晚9点过后不久，日本宪兵和军队即撤离南京路。
晚上7时30分，在先施公司百货商店前昏暗的街灯下，日本陆军代表与上海公共租界工部局警务处代表举行了一次临时会议，就南京路爆炸事件的解决条款达成一致。据悉，参加会谈的有日本陆军驻沪特务机关长楠本实隆大佐（Sanetaka Kusumoto，音译），他是日本总司令松井石根将军（Iwane Matsui）的代表，以及警务处处长F. W. 杰拉德（F. W. Gerrard）。副领事吉冈福亮（Foriake Yoshioka，音译）亦在场。

随着对工部局应采取的步骤达成完全一致，日军及宪兵从百货公司区域撤出。
昨晚日方人士称，商定的措施将 solely 由上海公共租界工部局警务处执行。
这次夜间会议是在街道上举行的，地点距离下午12时50分左右一名被日方称为中国人的青年投掷手榴弹、致使三名日本士兵、一名日本领事馆警察和一名英国警长受伤的地点仅几码之遥。

随着协议的达成，以及日本宪兵在该地区进行的调查结束，日军于晚上8时30分开始从该区撤离，并随即全部撤出。

普赖斯上校的交涉

美国海军陆战队第四团团长查尔斯·F. B. 普赖斯上校（Charles F. B. Price）向负责调查昨日午后南京路手榴弹事件的日军分队指挥官提出交涉，促使日军从慕尔路（Mohawk Road）撤回到虞洽卿路（Yu Ya Ching Road）。
普赖斯上校在其参谋人员的陪同下，于下午5点前不久出现在慕尔路现场，并告诉在场的日军指挥官，日军已深入美国海军陆战队的防区内部。他建议他们离开该防区。
该日军军官表示，他并未意识到其部队沿静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）推进了如此远的距离，因此随即下达了撤退命令。

造成不便

日军从虞洽卿路与南京路交叉口推进至慕尔路，给国际饭店和大基督教青年会（Foreign Y.M.C.A.）的居民造成了相当大的不便。在一段时间内，这两座大楼内的人员无法进出。
下午5时15分，这两处地点前的街道被清空，约10分钟后，东至虞洽卿路的区域内的日军也被清除。
上海公共租界工部局警务处接管了街道巡逻任务，除在该主干道有公务的人员外，行人不得沿静安寺路向北越过派克路（Park Road）。

一名落单士兵出现

当同伴后撤时，有一名落单的日本士兵未能及时撤离，他从一条小巷出来，发现街上已无其长官。他请求一名警察指引他返回虞洽卿路，该请求得到了满足。最后一次看到他时，他正沿着街道缓慢向北移动。
昨晚，日本调查组占据了从福建路到虞洽卿路的南京路路段。他们还控制了从九江路到北京路的虞洽卿路路段，并占据了从九江路到北京路的福建路路段。
日本大使馆发言人在昨晚告诉新闻记者和外国通讯员，日本当局“不打算利用这一事件谋取不当利益”。该发言人透露，在调查期间，将在该地区保持巡逻。

4名日本人受伤

凌晨12时50分，当手榴弹被投向一支路过的日军纵队时，包括三名士兵在内的四名日本人和一名英国警长受伤。据日方称，手榴弹是由一名中国青年从先施公司百货商店附近的位置投掷的。

这名年龄约为25岁的青年设法突破了广西路（Kwangse Road）的警戒线，并从那里投掷了爆炸物。
附近的一名中国巡捕立即向该男子开枪，击中其四处。该男子约一小时后死亡。
在昨晚的新闻发布会上，当被问及中国巡捕向该男子开枪的行为时，一位日本发言人宣称，该巡捕履行了其职责。
受伤的日本人为：
远藤文（Bun Endo，音译）二等兵，左髋部重伤。
板桥松五郎（Matsugero Itabashi，音译）二等兵，左腿轻伤。
川岛森田（Morita Kawashima，音译）二等兵，右腿轻伤。
日本领事馆警察吉冈敬二（Keiji Yoshioka，音译）警员，身中六弹，包括额头一处。
这三名士兵属于福井分队。该警察被指派护送日军通过租界。

督察亦受伤

上海公共租界工部局警务处督察约翰·麦克菲（John McPhee）当时靠近事件现场，手臂和腿部受轻伤。
吉冈警员的伤势相当严重，他目前在法国医院接受治疗，预计需留院六至七周才能恢复职务。
手榴弹在距离该警员站立处约一米的地方爆炸。
手榴弹的爆炸并未阻止日军游行，尽管确实引起了一阵短暂的骚动。在该特定路段行进的日军立即停止前进，并派出巡逻队在附近街道进行搜索。
现场的外国记者和其他外国人立即四处寻找掩护。日本巡逻队自己也迅速行动。

恢复行进

然而，日军主力随后不久恢复了行进，并于下午1时40分通过了外白渡桥（Garden Bridge）。
在从虹口区调来的部队增援下，日本军官和士兵接管了案件的调查工作，并逐渐将围观人群从南京路的东西两侧向后驱散。到下午4点，他们已在虞洽卿路、汉口路和福建路进行巡逻。他们在冈村大尉（Captain Okamura）和塚本诚大尉（Captain Makoto Tsukamoto）指挥下的日本宪兵的协助下进行行动。
日本宪兵官员、上海公共租界工部局警务处以及日本领事馆警察在现场进行了调查。

page_data.en:
The affair immediately precipitat-
ed a minor exodus from the area.
The many shops in the district
patrolled by the Japanese troops
were quietly boarded up by their
owners. Iron gates were swung
across the main entrances and no
one was allowed to leave the place.
Customers Caught
As a result hundreds of customers
of the Sincere, Wing On and Sun
Sun Department stores were caught
inside these places and were unable
to get out. They were allowed to
go after the Japanese troops had
been withdrawn.
Forty persons, mostly foreigners,
who were dining in the Sun Ya
Restaurant and were caught in that
building, were escorted out by the
Shanghai Municipal Police about 4
p.m.
A few women and children were
permitted to leave the area, but no
one was allowed to enter.
There were plenty of photograph-
ers on hand and the scenes that
occurred both during the bombing
and when the streets in the area
were being cleared were well photo-
graphed.
The man who allegedly threw the
bomb and who was shot by the
Chinese Police Constable was taken
in custody by the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Police and later by the Jap-
anese authorities.
The fellow was laid out on a
sidewalk along an alleyway at the
side of the Wing On Store and his
body was kept there most of the
afternoon. He died about an hour
after he was shot.
Newspapermen and photographers
clustered about the entrance of the
alleyway in an effort to get a look
at the man but were unsuccessful.
No pictures were permitted and no
one was allowed to get within 20
feet of the body.
Street Cleared
Shortly after 3 p.m., the Japanese
commenced clearing the street of
everybody. Men with fixed bayo-
nets were strung across the street
and everybody was pushed back.
A detachment of British troops
marched down the street from the
west and were permitted to pass
through the Japanese cordon. A
U.S. Marine motorcycle messenger
also was permitted to pass.
A few minutes later, a British
army mail truck came down the
street traveling toward the Bund
and was stopped and made to turn
around. Another American Marine
motorcycle messenger tried to get
through and also was stopped. After
that no exceptions were made in
the cases of anybody trying to pass
through the Japanese cordon.
Everybody was turned back.
Two machine-guns were planted
by the Japanese at the intersection
of Yu Ya Ching and Nanking Roads
and pointed in a westerly direction.
Traffic Disrupted
Traffic along Nanking Road was
badly disrupted as a result of the
blocking off of the street. Buses
were forced to turn about from
Fukien Road. They doubled back
to the Bund and resumed operations
along Avenue Edward VII. Trams
were forced to double back from
both sides of the cordon.
As a result of the loss of Nanking
Road to traffic, congestion was heavy
along Avenue Edward VII through-
out the evening.
Lieutenant Colonel Yuki Fukasori
was placed in command of the
Japanese troops in the department
store district, it was announced last
night.
It was reported in some circles
that the man who threw the grenade
was a Korean and not a Chinese.
A Japanese spokesman at the press
conference, however, stated that
while the man's name had not then
been established, it was known that
he was a Chinese.
page_data.zh:
这一事件立即导致该地区出现小规模的人口外流。
由日军巡逻的地区内的许多商店被店主悄悄用木板封住。铁门被关上挡住主要入口，任何人不得离开该地。
顾客被困

结果，永安公司和先施公司百货公司的数百名顾客被困在这些地方，无法外出。直到日军撤走后，他们才被允许离开。
约四十人，大多为外国人，当时正在新亚酒店（Sun Ya Restaurant）用餐并被困在该建筑内，于下午4点左右由上海公共租界工部局警务处护送出。
少数妇女和儿童被允许离开该地区，但任何人不得进入。
现场有许多摄影师，爆炸发生时以及该地区街道被清空时的场景都被很好地拍摄下来。
据称投掷炸弹并被中国巡捕击中的那名男子，先由上海公共租界工部局警务处拘留，后移交给日本当局。
该男子被平躺在永安公司旁边一条小巷的人行道上，他的尸体在那里停放了大半个下午。他在中枪约一小时后死亡。
新闻记者和摄影师聚集在小巷入口处，试图看一眼该男子，但未成功。不允许拍照，任何人不得靠近尸体20英尺以内。
街道清空

下午3点后不久，日本人开始清空街道上的所有人。端着固定刺刀的士兵横跨街道排开，所有人被向后驱赶。
一队英军从西边沿街道行进，被允许穿过日本的封锁线。一名美国海军陆战队摩托车传令兵也被允许通过。
几分钟后，一辆英国陆军邮车沿街道驶向外滩，被拦停并被要求掉头。另一名美国海军陆战队摩托车传令兵试图通过，也被拦停。此后，对于任何试图穿过日本封锁线的人，不再有任何例外。所有人都被折返。
日本人在虞洽卿路与南京路的交叉口部署了两挺机枪，枪口指向西方。
交通中断

由于街道被封锁，南京路沿线的交通受到严重干扰。公共汽车被迫从福建路掉头。它们折返外滩，并在爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）恢复运营。有轨电车被迫从封锁线的两侧折返。
由于南京路交通中断，整个晚上爱多亚路的拥堵非常严重。
昨晚宣布，深堀幸雄中佐（Lieutenant Colonel Yuki Fukasori，音译）被任命为百货公司地区日军的指挥官。
有消息称，投掷手榴弹的人是朝鲜人而非中国人。
然而，在新闻发布会上的日本发言人表示，虽然该男子的姓名当时尚未确定，但已知他是中国人。

page_data.en:
JAPANESE STOP BRITISH TROOPS
泰康明
A company of the Royal Fusiliers marching down Nanking Road
at 2.20 p.m. yesterday past the scene of the bombing, which took
place an hour-and-a-half earlier were stopped for several minutes by
Japanese soldiers. Permission to march through was granted after
the matter was referred to an officer.
World News Photo.

CAR STOPPED ON NANKING ROAD
A British military car with an officer sitting in it was stopped along
Nanking Road by Japanese soldiers yesterday while the investigation
into the missile throwing incident was proceeding. After ascertaining
as to who was in the car it was allowed to proceed.
World News Photo.

日军拦截英军
泰康明
昨天下午2时20分，皇家燧发枪团（Royal Fusiliers）的一个连队沿南京路行进，经过一个半小时前发生爆炸的现场时，被日本士兵拦截数分钟。在向一名军官请示后，获准通过。
世界新闻照片社（World News Photo）。

汽车在南京路被拦停
昨天，在对投掷爆炸物事件进行调查期间，一辆载有一名军官的英国军用汽车在南京路被日本士兵拦停。在查明车内人员身份后，获准继续前行。
